news.Title: nLight (LASR) Beats Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
news.Content:
nLight (LASR) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.16 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.06 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.08 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +166.67%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this laser maker would post earnings of $0.14 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.15, delivering a surprise of +7.14%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

nLight, which belongs to the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, posted revenues of $73.76 million for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 8.55%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $66.74 million. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

nLight shares have lost about 12.1% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 12.3%.

What's Next for nLight?

While nLight has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for nLight was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $0.11 on $73.2 million in revenues for the coming quarter and $0.52 on $303.89 million in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Story Continues

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Electronics - Semiconductors is currently in the top 30% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

Another stock from the same industry, Marvell Technology (MRVL), has yet to report results for the quarter ended October 2026.

This chipmaker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $1.10 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +44.7%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.1% higher over the last 30 days to the current level.

Marvell Technology's revenues are expected to be $3.16 billion, up 52.2% from the year-ago quarter.

news.Title: Why Marvell Stock Is Falling Today
news.Content:
Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRVL) stock is down 13.4% as of 2:42 p.m. ET on Thursday, Nov. 5, after Democrats' midterm victory set off a sell-off in chip and AI infrastructure stocks .

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) and the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) are down 3.9% and 5.0%, respectively.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Why Marvell stock is falling after the midterms

Investors are fleeing anything tied to AI data centers two days after Democrats flipped both houses of the U.S. Congress and won several key governorships.

Many Democrats ran on a platform that included increased oversight of the AI industry, with the party's new governors in Texas, Ohio, and Georgia -- major AI data center states -- promising construction moratoriums.

Marvell sells the networking chips that move data around inside those data centers -- it sits right in the blast zone.

Image source: Getty Images.

How Marvell's Lumentum deal could dilute shareholders

But this comes just days after an all-stock deal was announced Monday to buy Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) -- an AI photonics maker -- worth $115 billion. That could lead to significant dilution for Marvell stock. But it also means that as Marvell stock drops, the value of the shares it is offering Lumentum falls as well. There's a risk the deal falls apart or the terms get renegotiated, and Marvell shareholders see even more dilution.

news.Title: Wedbush Isn’t So Sure the Marvell-Lumentum Deal Will Really Happen. Here’s Why.
news.Content:
Semiconductor giant Marvell Technology (MRVL) has pitched an acquisition of optical and photonic products manufacturer Lumentum Holdings (LITE). This brings Lumentum's lasers, optical transceivers, and optical circuit switches (OCS) to Marvell's switching, electrical and optical interconnects, and custom XPUs. While the strategic rationale is sound, investors did not like the deal.

The $115 billion all-stock acquisition announcement led to a 12.7% intraday drop in MRVL stock and an 18.6% decline in LITE stock on Nov. 2. Marvell shareholders voiced concerns about share dilution, as Lumentum holders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, leaving them with 33% of the combined company. That is expected to materially increase Marvell's share count and dilute existing holders. Lumentum shareholders are concerned because the deal would convert their ownership from a stand-alone AI optics company to Marvell shares.

Amid all this, Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson believes the deal, set to close in the first half of 2028, might not actually happen. Beyond the regulatory approval process and China's reluctance to approve major technology mergers, lasers are in tight supply, with Lumentum currently supplying Marvell's competitors.

As the deal drives sentiment around the two stocks, let's take a closer look at them.

The One Carrying Out the Acquisition: Marvell Technology (MRVL)

Marvell is a fabless semiconductor company that designs, develops, and sells data-infrastructure chips for data centers, cloud computing, networking, storage, security, and communications. Headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, the company has a market capitalization of $154.05 billion.

Marvell's stock has risen over the past year mainly because investors see it as a major beneficiary of hyperscalers' spending on AI data centers. Over the past 52 weeks, MRVL stock has gained 48%, while it has risen 62% year-to-date (YTD). The company's shares reached a 52-week high of $329.88 on June 18, but are down 58% from that level. However, the stock has dropped 37% over the past five days, mainly due to investor skepticism about the Lumentum deal and a broader selloff in chipmakers and AI stocks.

Story Continues

Despite the recent selloff, Marvell's stock still doesn't come cheap. On a forward-adjusted basis, its price-to-earnings (non-GAAP) ratio of 56.37x is higher than the industry average of 21.21x.

In the second quarter of fiscal 2027 (quarter ended Aug. 1), Marvell reported strong results driven by demand in its data center portfolio, in which the company reported a 46% year-over-year (YoY) growth. Its AI-related bookings remained robust, which is expected to continue creating tailwinds for its top line. Data centers now make up 79% of its revenue. The company's total revenue increased 37% YoY to $2.74 billion. Its adjusted EPS rose 40% from the prior-year period to $0.94.

Wall Street analysts are robustly optimistic about Marvell's future earnings. They expect the company's EPS to climb 27.4% YoY to $0.79 for the third quarter of fiscal 2027. For fiscal 2027, EPS is projected to surge 41.2% to $3.05, followed by a 99.7% growth to $6.09 in fiscal 2028.

Marvell is gaining praise on Wall Street, with analysts awarding it a consensus "Strong Buy" rating overall. Of the 39 analysts rating MRVL stock, 28 have given it a "Strong Buy" rating, three analysts rated it a "Moderate Buy," and eight took a middle-of-the-road approach with a "Hold" rating. The consensus price target of $317.05 represents an 131% upside from current levels. The Street-high price target of $450 implies a 229% upside.

The One Being Acquired: Lumentum Holdings (LITE)

Lumentum designs and manufactures optical and photonic technologies, including high-performance lasers, modules, and optical subsystems. Its products support data-center connectivity for AI and cloud computing, telecommunications networks, industrial manufacturing, and sensing applications. Headquartered in San Jose, California, Lumentum operates research, manufacturing, and sales facilities worldwide. The company has a market capitalization of $61.68 billion.

Due to explosive AI optics demand, Lumentum's stock has gained 126% over the past 52 weeks, while it has been up 43% YTD. Like Marvell, Lumentum's stock is also deep in the red, down 43% over the past five days due to both the same skepticism regarding the deal and the aforementioned broader selloff hitting most AI-related stocks. LITE stock reached a 52-week high of $1,143 on Oct. 9, but is down 54% from that level.

On a forward-adjusted basis, Lumentum's stock has a price-to-earnings (non-GAAP) ratio of 34.36x, which is higher than the industry average of 21.21x.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (quarter ended Sept. 26), Lumentum reported growth across all businesses, with pump lasers and OCS being the leading contributors. The company also reported greater OCS demand visibility, positioning optical switching as a multi-billion-dollar annual revenue stream. The company's total revenue increased 136.5% YoY to $1.26 billion, while its non-GAAP EPS increased from $1.10 to $4.57 over the same period.

Wall Street analysts are strongly optimistic about Lumentum's future earnings trajectory. They expect the company's EPS to climb 271% YoY to $4.60 for the current quarter. For fiscal 2027, EPS is projected to surge 143.5% to $19.80, followed by a 67.8% growth to $33.23 in fiscal 2028.

Lumentum's stock has become a popular name on Wall Street, with analysts awarding it a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating. Of the 25 analysts rating LITE stock, 17 analysts have rated it a "Strong Buy," one analyst rated it a "Moderate Buy," and seven analysts gave a "Hold" rating. The consensus price target of $1,094.72 represents a 107% upside from current levels. Moreover, the Street-high price target of $1,500 indicates a 184% upside.

news.Title: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold AXTI Stock After Its Strong Q3 Results?
news.Content:
AXT, Inc. AXTI is emerging as a key beneficiary of AI data-center networking upgrades following a breakout third quarter. Revenues climbed 162% year over year to a record $73.4 million, while non-GAAP earnings swung to 41 cents per share from a loss of 3 cents a year earlier. Non-GAAP gross margin jumped to 56.1% from 22.4%, reflecting higher indium phosphide (InP) volumes, favorable product mix and improved manufacturing productivity.

However, the stock's remarkable rally has raised the bar for further gains. AXTI has surged 190.8% year to date compared with an 11.4% rise for the Zacks Electronics – Semiconductors industry and a 9.1% gain for the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector.

AXTI stock has also outperformed several major semiconductor peers, including Marvell Technology MRVL, FormFactor FORM and Amkor Technology AMKR. Year to date, shares of Marvell Technology have jumped 88.1% and FormFactor has advanced 52.9%, while Amkor Technology has declined 9.6%.

YTD Price Return Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Such outperformance raises an important question: Is AXTI still worth buying at current levels, or should investors book profits or continue holding the stock? Let's take a closer look at its growth prospects, valuation and key risks.

AXTI's InP Franchise and Capacity Expansion Underpin Growth

AXTI's InP sales reached $54.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, representing roughly 74% of revenues. Its substrates support lasers and photodetectors used in 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers, increasingly important as AI clusters demand faster interconnects.

Demand for high-quality InP substrates remains ahead of supply, providing AXTI with considerable growth opportunities. The company surpassed its initial 2026 capacity-doubling goal in August and is progressing toward larger 4-inch and 6-inch substrates. Advanced crystal-growth furnaces and low-defect materials could lift output, selling prices and margins.

Backlog surpassed $500 million, spanning multiyear agreements, shorter contracts and spot orders. A Lumentum supply agreement brought a $43.5 million wafer prepayment, strengthening demand visibility; importantly, the payment remains a liability until shipments occur. Management aims to double InP capacity again in 2027, backed by investments in raw-material sourcing and production efficiency.

AXTI's technological positioning also differentiates it within the semiconductor supply chain. Marvell Technology develops optical DSPs that enable high-speed links, FormFactor supplies semiconductor testing solutions and Amkor Technology provides semiconductor packaging and testing services. While all three companies can benefit from AI infrastructure investments, AXTI's exposure to specialized InP substrate production gives it a more concentrated opportunity tied to optical connectivity.

Story Continues

AXTI's Earnings Outlook Signals Growth

For the fourth quarter of 2026, AXTI expects non-GAAP EPS of 57-59 cents and GAAP EPS of 56-58 cents. Management also anticipates generating approximately $90 million in revenues from substrate products and raw materials for which export permits have already been secured or are not required.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for AXTI's fourth-quarter 2026 earnings is pegged at 56 cents per share, compared with a loss of 5 cents a year ago. The full-year 2026 EPS consensus stands at $1.17 per share, followed by $2.47 for 2027, indicating significant growth. The consensus estimates have moved higher over the past 30 and 60 days, signaling improving analyst expectations.

China Exposure and Capacity Execution Remain Risks

Most of AXTI's manufacturing operations are based in China, making export permits and U.S.-China tensions material swing factors. Shipments requiring additional approvals may be delayed even when demand is strong. The company must also execute a rapid capacity ramp without sacrificing yields, while rising raw-material costs could pressure profitability. Backlog includes spot orders and shorter commitments, so it is not equivalent to guaranteed revenues.

Growth also brings financing and ownership trade-offs. The diluted weighted-average share count increased to 65.9 million in the reported third quarter from 43.8 million a year earlier. A planned investment of up to $545 million into subsidiary Tongmei would finance expansion but, if fully completed, lower AXT's ownership to approximately 73.4%. Compared with Marvell Technology's broader product portfolio, FormFactor's test-equipment exposure and Amkor Technology's packaging footprint, AXTI is particularly sensitive to InP production and export constraints.

AXTI's Rich Valuation Raises the Bar

AXTI's valuation presents a significant hurdle for investors. The stock trades at 24.43X forward 12-month Price/Earnings (P/E) compared with 8.77X for the Zacks Electronics – Semiconductors industry, representing approximately 2.8 times the industry's valuation multiple. AXTI also carries a Value Score of F, indicating overvaluation relative to fundamentals.

This premium is particularly notable following the stock's 193% year-to-date appreciation. While strong earnings growth and the expanding InP opportunity provide fundamental support, much of AXTI's anticipated growth may already be reflected in its share price. Consequently, any delays in export approvals, capacity expansion or wafer-yield improvements could weigh on investor sentiment and put pressure on the stock's valuation.

AXTI's P/E Ratio (F12M)

Conclusion: Hold AXTI Stock

AXTI's record profitability, accelerating InP demand, expanding production capacity and substantial backlog support a compelling multiyear growth narrative. The company's stronger fourth-quarter earnings guidance and continued investment in larger-diameter substrates further strengthen the company's long-term prospects.

Nevertheless, export dependence, share dilution, capacity-ramp uncertainty and a sizable valuation premium argue against chasing the stock after its 193% surge. Investors may consider holding AXTI while monitoring export approvals, 4-inch and 6-inch production yields, backlog conversion and actual earnings-estimate revisions for further gains.

AXTI currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: MRVL's Networking Business Grows on the Back of AI: What's Ahead?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology MRVL has been supporting the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure market with a broad portfolio of networking, interconnect and optical technologies designed to address the rising bandwidth requirements of next-generation data centers. As hyperscalers deploy increasingly large AI clusters, the demand for high-speed connectivity between servers, racks, accelerators and geographically distributed data centers is growing substantially.

Marvell's optical interconnect business remains a significant contributor to its AI-driven growth. Optical DSPs are critical components in high-speed optical communication systems, enabling the transmission of data at increasingly higher bandwidths while maintaining signal integrity. During the second quarter of fiscal 2027, demand for Marvell's 800G optical DSPs remained strong, while its 1.6T optical DSP business ramped rapidly.

Marvell's scale-out networking business is also gaining traction through its high-capacity switching portfolio. The company remains on track to more than double its scale-out switching revenues in fiscal 2027, driven by the expanding adoption of its 51.2T switching products across a broader customer base. These switches facilitate high-bandwidth connectivity between racks and servers within data centers, helping AI clusters scale efficiently.

Beyond traditional data center networking, Marvell is targeting the emerging scale-across opportunity as hyperscalers build larger AI clusters spanning multiple data centers. These architectures require high-bandwidth connections between geographically distributed facilities, creating demand for advanced data center interconnect technologies. MRVL is also pursuing the emerging scale-up networking market, which involves connecting AI accelerators within increasingly large computing domains.

Although customers are initially deploying copper interconnects for scale-up networking, management expects the limitations of copper in terms of reach and bandwidth to increasingly drive adoption of optical interconnect technologies as AI cluster sizes expand. Management also expects the adoption of 1.6T solutions to accelerate further in fiscal 2028 as hyperscalers upgrade their data center networking infrastructure to accommodate growing AI workloads.

How Competitors Fare Against MRVL Stock

MRVL faces stiff competition in the AI networking and custom silicon space from Broadcom AVGO and Advanced Micro Devices AMD.

Broadcom is a leader in the domain of custom silicon solutions for data centers. Broadcom's advanced 3.5D XDSiP packaging platform is critical to ensure the performance and efficiency of custom AI XPUs.

Story Continues

Advanced Micro Devices is another established player in the custom silicon solutions and AI accelerator market. Advanced Micro Devices offers semi-custom SoCs and Instinct Accelerators to power data centers.

MRVL's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Shares of Marvell Technology have surged 88.1% year to date compared with the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry's growth of 11.4%.

news.Title: Jim Cramer sends clear signal on Apple and Palantir stock
news.Content:
Jim Cramer thinks investors have gone too far.

As the tech slump dragged into a new week, the CNBC host said in a post on X that the negativity around Marvell, Apple, and Palantir "is pretty thick," adding, "No matter what they say, it isn't enough."

He made the remark as all three stocks slid on Nov. 2.

His comments landed in a rough market. Chip and memory stocks have lost about $3.7 trillion in market value since Oct. 6, and Intel suffered its worst day since 1974 on Oct. 30, falling nearly 29% after a disappointing forecast.

The chip group shed more than $400 billion on Nov. 2 alone, as reported by Yahoo Finance . In a market this nervous, even good news is getting sold.

Marvell's mega-deal spooks investors

Marvell took the hardest hit. Its shares fell sharply on Nov. 2 after it announced an all-stock deal to buy Lumentum for $115 billion, and the stock has pulled back significantly since reports of the deal surfaced on Oct. 28.

Also read: Jim Cramer has a new way of thinking about the biggest tech stocks

The size of the bet explains part of the worry. Lumentum holders will get 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they own, leaving them with roughly a third of the combined company, and the deal is more than 10 times bigger than Marvell's previous largest purchase.

Marvell CEO Matt Murphy acknowledged that in a stock deal, the buyer's share price is the real price tag. "You take more risk when you do it," he said .

Murphy is not backing away. Marvell wants Lumentum's optical connectivity technology, which links the chips used to train and run large language models.

He called the deal "a double-down on supporting Nvidia, who is the ecosystem leader in this area." Meanwhile, investors appeared to view Marvell as overpaid, sending Lumentum down almost 19% after its stock had soared more than 450% over the past year.

The deal's final value will depend on Marvell's share price when it closes, according to CNBC . The deal is not expected to close until the first half of 2028.

Apple beats, but its memory costs bite

Apple's numbers were good. Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue hit $114.48 billion and earnings came to $2.10 a share, both ahead of Wall Street's forecasts.

It wrapped up what Apple called its strongest fiscal year on record. Even so, the stock drifted lower after hours, with investors fixated on slowing growth.

What really spooked investors was the guidance. Apple expects a gross margin of 45% to 46% in the December quarter, down from 47.9%, and blamed most of that drop on pricier memory chips, Reuters reported .

Story Continues

Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, pointed out the irony in a post on X : The same DRAM boom helping Micron and SK Hynix is pinching Apple right as it leans into on-device AI.

CEO John Ternus called the memory situation "unprecedented" on his first earnings call, MacRumors noted. Still, Apple expects December-quarter revenue to grow 7% to 10%, which would make it the company's best quarter on record.

Services also hit a quarterly record of $31.6 billion, though Mac and iPad supply will stay tight.

The memory squeeze is good news for chipmakers. SK Hynix said DRAM prices rose in the high 20s percent from the second quarter, helping it post a record operating profit, while DRAM shipments grew about 10%, according to its Q3 2026 earnings .

What fills a memory maker's pockets drains Apple's margins.

Palantir's bookings spark doubts

Palantir also beat on both lines in the third quarter. Revenue came in at $2.31 billion against estimates of $2.18 billion, and adjusted earnings were 44 cents a share against 41 cents, yet the stock closed 3% lower.

The growth itself was huge. It was Palantir's first quarter above $2 billion. Revenue rose 96% from a year earlier, and U.S. commercial revenue climbed 148% to $984 million, passing the $953 million from U.S. government work for the first time, as reported by TechCrunch .

Investors zeroed in on bookings instead. U.S. commercial total contract value fell to $1.46 billion from a record $2.13 billion in the prior quarter. Boloor said in a separate post on X that he genuinely does not think anyone knows how high the ceiling is for this business.

More Jim Cramer:

Jim Cramer says Scott Bessent is fighting a flood with one finger

Jim Cramer spots something investors may be missing on Wall Street

Jim Cramer calls one major data center play a no-brainer buy

Karp had an explanation for the slowdown. He said customers are adopting faster but signing shorter contracts, with "an ability to expand that contract dramatically," and Palantir raised its full-year revenue guidance.

That suggests the slowdown may reflect how deals are being structured rather than weaker demand.

Related: Jim Cramer's net worth: How much does 'Mad Money's' stock-picking superhost make?

AI spending fears hang over tech

The bigger backdrop is anxiety about AI spending. Last week's two-day rout erased hundreds of billions in market value from Alphabet and Intel as investors punished cash-draining AI investment.

That set a sour tone heading into the Nov. 2 session.

Alphabet's report showed why. Its free cash flow came in at negative $9.07 billion in the third quarter, following a negative $5.86 billion in the second, while capital spending reached about $51.4 billion.

The stock then suffered its worst post-earnings sell-off on record, though some managers still see value, citing strong Google Cloud growth and a rapidly expanding order backlog.

That is the kind of disconnect Cramer is pointing to at Apple, Palantir, and Marvell, where solid results are being drowned out by fear.

news.Title: Credo and Oracle Drive AI Optical Innovation: Is CRDO Set to Benefit?
news.Content:
Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd . CRDO recently achieved a breakthrough with Oracle ORCL by securing Open Compute Project (OCP) approval for two new specifications designed to improve optical connectivity and reliability in AI data centers. The development highlights Credo's growing role in addressing a critical challenge of maintaining reliable, high-speed connections across increasingly massive computing clusters facing next-generation AI infrastructure. The partnership with Oracle is likely to strengthen its position in the optical connectivity ecosystem while supporting the broader industry's transition toward more reliable AI infrastructure.

Established in January 2026, the workstream is co-led by Credo and Oracle. Its primary objective is to establish a common software interface that enables optical transceivers and host systems to exchange detailed connection health information. The two approved specifications standardize optical link-health monitoring, telemetry sharing, event tracking and automated fault responses, while enabling optical DSPs to exchange out-of-band information without disrupting network traffic. Credo contributed its ZeroFlap host specification as the technical foundation. Developed with input from the broader OCP Community, the standards could support wider adoption among hardware manufacturers, data center operators and technology providers.

Furthermore, CRDO is helping shape next-generation AI data center connectivity through an OCP workstream targeting 2027 approval for micro-emitter optics specifications. It recently announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream within the OCP Community. The initiative brings together optical technology providers, connectivity specialists and a leading hyperscaler to set specifications for a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. Also, in September, Credo launched 224G ZeroFlap optical transceivers supporting 1.6T port speeds and AI architectures.

However, competition in high-speed connectivity from key semiconductor and optical networking players like Marvell Technology MRVL and Astera Labs ALAB remains intense.

CRDO vs. Rivals: Assessing Its Connectivity Advantage

Marvell's acquisition of Lumentum aims to create a leading AI connectivity provider by combining complementary expertise in optical, photonics and electrical technologies. The deal is expected to accelerate innovation in NPO, CPO and integrated AI data center solutions, expand manufacturing capacity and strengthen end-to-end product offerings. With a projected $550 billion addressable market by 2030, the combined company expects to generate more than $1 billion in synergies, accelerate growth and strengthen its competitive position through deeper integration and scale. Expanded NVIDIA partnership aligns Marvell's roadmap more closely with next-generation AI architectures, extending its reach across optics, NVLink Fusion integration and AI-RAN platforms.

Story Continues

It plans to begin sampling with hyperscalers and OEMs, with initial revenue expected in late 2027 and CPO volumes ramping in 2028–2029. With a projected $40 billion scale-up optical interconnect market by 2030, Astera aims to capture more content per XPU through vertically integrated optical components, engines and fabric switches. For the fourth quarter, management forecast revenue of $730-$750 million, noting continued supply constraints in wafers, power and memory and limited visibility into customer deployment timelines.

news.Title: ASML vs. Marvell Technology: Which Artificial Intelligence Stock Is a Better Buy Going into 2027?
news.Content:
The race for better artificial intelligence continues to reshape the market, making investors choose between equipment giants and chip designers. Should you buy ASML (NASDAQ:ASML) or Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) today?

ASML provides the complex lithography systems used by the world's leading foundries to print the most advanced microchips. Marvell specializes in infrastructure solutions, connecting and moving massive amounts of data across cloud and carrier networks. Both companies are pivotal to the future of semiconductor technology, but they occupy very different rungs on the industry ladder.

The case for ASML

ASML manufactures the lithography systems that are essential for the production of advanced microchips found in everything from smartphones to data centers. It is currently the sole supplier of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines, which its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, notes are critical for cost-effective microchip scaling. The company serves the global semiconductor stocks ecosystem by delivering hardware and software for EUV and cheaper deep ultraviolet (DUV) applications.

In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, revenue reached $36.7 billion, representing a growth of 15.6% compared with the prior fiscal year. This expansion in the top line helped the company generate a net income of $10.8 billion. The net margin, which measures the percentage of revenue remaining after all expenses are paid, reached 29.4% during this period.

According to its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 0.2x shows the company uses very little borrowed money relative to its equity. The current ratio of approximately 1.3x indicates it maintains sufficient short-term assets to cover immediate liabilities. Free cash flow, which is the cash left over after accounting for capital expenditures, reached $12.4 billion for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025.

The case for Marvell Technology

Marvell Technology designs data infrastructure solutions that power artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and automotive industrial end markets across the globe. The company reported in its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, that its revenue is highly concentrated among a limited number of buyers. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as one distributor represented nearly 37% of revenue and a single direct customer accounted for roughly 14%.

In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, revenue reached $8.2 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 42.1%. This sharp increase in sales helped the company achieve a net income of $2.7 billion. The net margin for the period reached 32.6%, reflecting a significant improvement compared with the losses reported in the prior fiscal year.

Story Continues

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio of roughly 0.3x indicates a healthy balance between debt and equity. The current ratio of approximately 2.0x measures its ability to cover short-term obligations, and free cash flow for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, was nearly $1.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented 33.8% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

ASML faces potential volatility in the global chip market, where cycles of high demand for new equipment can be followed by periods of overcapacity. Geopolitical tensions also pose a significant threat, as trade restrictions on high-end lithography equipment can limit sales to certain geographic regions. Additionally, the extreme complexity of its machines means any production delays or technical hurdles in next-generation systems could impact its long-term growth trajectory.

Marvell Technology faces risks from significant revenue concentration, as a few large customers account for a majority of its annual sales. Strategic and integration risks are heightened by large-scale acquisitions, notably the announced $115 billion all-stock acquisition of Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE). Additionally, the company faces intense competition from Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) and potential supply chain disruptions due to the geographic concentration of its manufacturing partners.

Valuation comparison

ASML appears more affordably valued based on its Forward P/E and its P/S ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

ASML and Marvell Technology are both great stocks to own for exposure to the artificial intelligence boom. The former is an attractive AI stock since it holds a legal monopoly over the EUV lithography machines needed to construct AI chips, as competitors have not been able to successfully replicate the technology at scale. However, if I had to choose between these two, I would invest in Marvell.

Not only did Marvell report 42% year-over-year revenue growth in its 2026 fiscal year (FY), in its Investor Day held on Oct. 6, management set a FY 2031 target of $70 billion to $90 billion in sales. That's incredible growth compared to FY 2026's $8.2 billion, and indicates the company is seeing strong customer demand for its AI solutions.

That's where Marvell's bid to acquire Lumentum comes in. Lumentum reported fiscal Q1 revenue of $1.3 billion on Nov. 2, which represents a jaw-dropping 137% year-over-year increase. Its optical connectivity offerings enable rapid data transmission, a critical feature for data-hungry AI systems.

Marvell's acquisition caused its share price to fall, as Wall Street weighed the dilution risk of the all-stock deal. This creates an opportunity to pick up Marvell shares on the dip, as I believe Marvell's addition of Lumentum makes the company stronger over the long run.

news.Title: Is Broadcom Stock a Buy After Marvell's $115 Billion Deal?
news.Content:
On Nov. 2, Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) agreed to buy Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE), a maker of lasers and optical transceivers, in an all-stock deal. The firms put Lumentum's enterprise value (its stock market value plus debt, minus cash) at $115 billion, using both stocks' Oct. 28 closing prices.

Marvell says the combination creates a category leader in artificial intelligence (AI) connectivity -- the chips and optical parts that send data between AI processors.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) knows the business well. The chip designer sells custom AI accelerators, Ethernet switches, and optical components for AI data centers. But its stock dipped only about 1% on Nov. 2, while Marvell shares slid about 13%.

At roughly $335 as I write, Broadcom stock trades about 30% under its June 2 record close of $481.57. When I last wrote about the company on Oct. 28, with shares near $342, I said I'd consider buying a little at a time.

Does a bigger rival change that?

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Marvell is building a bigger rival

Marvell already designs custom AI chips, plus network switches and the electrical and optical interconnect chips that link AI systems together. Lumentum brings high-performance lasers and optical transceivers, along with its own compound semiconductor manufacturing.

Broadcom competes in most of those markets. It designs custom AI accelerators for six customers, including Alphabet's Google and Anthropic. The chips are made for one customer's AI work, as an alternative to general-purpose graphics processing units (GPUs).

Broadcom also sells Tomahawk Ethernet switches. On its fiscal third-quarter earnings call on Sept. 2, CEO Hock Tan said the company had just finished designing Tomahawk 7, which he called the industry's first 200-terabit-per-second Ethernet switch.

And Broadcom makes lasers, too.

"[D]emand for lasers ... is far surpassing supply out there in the industry," Tan said on the call. He added that Broadcom holds "a fairly substantial share of this market."

Put simply, Lumentum's lasers sell into a market where buyers can't currently get enough of them. Sure, shortages like this don't tend to last. But I think it makes the deal more of a long-term threat to Broadcom than a short-term one. A bigger rival could matter more when supply catches up to demand and buyers start shopping harder on price.

Story Continues

Broadcom's AI sales are still accelerating

Showing how far ahead Broadcom's AI business is, its AI semiconductor revenue hit $16.7 billion in fiscal Q3 (the quarter ended Aug. 2), up 221% year over year. Marvell's total revenue for its own quarter ended Aug. 1 was $2.74 billion, or around one-sixth as much.

And Broadcom's AI growth has picked up every quarter this year. AI revenue growth climbed from 106% in fiscal Q1 to 143% in fiscal Q2, then to 221% in fiscal Q3. Management guided for 236% year-over-year growth, to $21.7 billion, in fiscal Q4, which ended Nov. 1.

Broadcom has its own $115 billion number, and it means something else: the company's forecast for AI semiconductor revenue in fiscal 2027, the fiscal year that started this week.

This would double the almost $58 billion Broadcom expected for fiscal 2026. And Tan said on the Sept. 2 call that the company's already locked in the supply to get there.

"Our demand actually exceeds this outlook, and we will work to improve supply," he said.

The deal won't affect that year directly. Marvell expects the acquisition to close in the first half of calendar 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approvals. So Broadcom's fiscal 2027 will probably be over before the combined company even exists.

Time to buy?

Investors can buy this growth for less than they'd pay for the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC). Broadcom trades at around 17 times analysts' consensus earnings estimate for fiscal 2027.

This compares to about 18.7 times forward earnings for the S&P 500 overall.

True, Broadcom relies on a few very big AI customers, and a stronger Marvell could offer these customers another place to shop for custom chips and lasers. But this option is probably years away. And Broadcom's AI business is already several times the size of Marvell's whole company.

Ultimately, the deal doesn't change my take on Broadcom. It does make the company's laser and switching sales worth watching more closely once the combined company exists.

Meanwhile, the stock is a bit cheaper than when I last wrote about it, and nothing in the deal affects Broadcom's fiscal 2027 outlook. I'd still consider buying shares at this price.

news.Title: What a $115 Billion Deal to Buy Lumentum Really Means for Marvell Stock Investors
news.Content:
Semiconductor company Marvell Technology (MRVL) is all set to acquire Lumentum (LITE), a leading supplier of optical and photonic technologies, for $115 billion in an all-stock deal. Under the terms of the agreement, Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 shares of Marvell for each share of LITE stock they own. Marvell shareholders will own 67% of the combined company, while the rest will be held by Lumentum shareholders.

Marvell investors made their displeasure about the development clear, with shares ending almost 13% lower on Nov. 2 and down again today. They appear to believe the price tag of the deal is too high while the heavy dilution is also undesirable. Notably, the $115 billion consideration is an 86% premium to Lumentum's current market capitalization of $61.6 billion.

More News from Barchart

Why Investors Should Load Up on Google Stock Now

Billionaire Mark Cuban Says the Hardest Part of Fixing Health Costs Isn't the CEOs or Insurance Companies, 'Employees Fight Any Change'

Coca-Cola Pays Warren Buffett's Berkshire $848 Million a Year as Jim Cramer Says Buy KO Stock

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

However, Marvell management believes that the deal has the potential to result in cost savings of more than $1 billion. "The companies that move first and help define this transition will set the standard for decades to come," said CEO Matt Murphy, describing the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure market's focus on optical connectivity as a "once in a generation" opportunity. "By bringing together two leaders with highly complementary technologies, exceptional talent and specialized manufacturing capabilities, we intend to help shape the next era of AI connectivity and create exceptional stockholder value."

About Marvell Technology

Founded in 1995, Marvell is an AI infrastructure company centered on data-center connectivity, custom silicon, optical interconnects, switching, and storage. Its custom silicon business in particular includes custom AI accelerators, XPUs, networking chips, storage and memory controllers, and data-center interconnect products. Marvell has an impressive customer base that includes Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), and Alphabet (GOOGL), among others.

Marvell currently commands a market cap of $150.8 billion, with MRVL stock up an impressive 86% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. Notably, the stock also offers a modest dividend yield of 0.14%.

So, keeping the immediate market reaction aside, how will Marvell's impending acquisition of Lumentum impact its operations? Let's take a closer look.

Story Continues

Lumentum Is Legit for Marvell in the Long Haul

One rationale being bandied about the deal is that Marvell will gain access to Lumentum's expertise in optical transceivers, which allows for faster data transfer with less power. However, Marvell is buying more than faster optical transceivers. The bigger ambition of the deal is to control more of the technology connecting AI processors — from custom silicon and networking chips to lasers, optical modules, and optical circuit switches.

Notably, Marvell wants to design the electrical and optical signal chain together rather than optimize individual components separately. Bringing its silicon photonics, switching, and custom processors together with Lumentum's lasers and optical manufacturing could reduce engineering friction, simplify customer qualification, and shorten development cycles, resulting in the development of a vertically integrated semiconductor player that is harder to replace once its technologies are incorporated into a customer's design.

Meanwhile, Lumentum also brings indium phosphide capabilities and specialized laser production that complement Marvell's semiconductor design strengths. Additionally, optical circuit switching provides a separate growth opportunity beyond transceivers.

On Nov. 2, amid its first-quarter fiscal 2027 results, Lumentum said that optical circuit switch (OCS) demand visibility could support a business generating several billion dollars annually. Management also disclosed a second major win involving optics placed near or alongside processors, supported by purchase commitments exceeding $5 billion. Those commitments give the Marvell acquisition thesis more substance than a broad forecast for rising AI traffic alone.

Finally, with Lumentum, Marvell will be able to offer potential customers a more complete alternative to its larger peer and biggest competitor, Broadcom (AVGO). However, integration also creates a potential channel conflict. Customers that currently buy components from independent suppliers may hesitate if their supplier becomes a broader competitor. Marvell must preserve those relationships while pursuing more integrated sales.

Marvell Reports a Super Q2

Before examining Marvell's Q2 figures, we should look at the company's updated commentary on fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 revenue. Marvell raised its revenue outlook for both years, now projecting fiscal 2027 revenue of $12 billion and fiscal 2028 revenue of $18 billion, up from previous guidance of $11.5 billion and $16.5 billion, respectively. Within the fiscal 2028 outlook, Marvell anticipates data-center revenue growth of 60%, underscoring continued strength in the largest segment of the AI infrastructure buildout.

That momentum was visible in the latest quarterly results as well. Marvell reported record net revenue of $2.74 billion in Q2 fiscal 2027, representing a 37% increase from the prior year. Although that absolute figure set a new high, the growth rate lagged Broadcom, which recorded a 48% rise in its corresponding Q2 results. Meanwhile, Marvell's data-center revenue advanced 46% year-over-year (YOY) to $2.17 billion in Q2.

Gross margins contracted modestly to 58.9% from 59.4% in the year-ago period as stock-based compensation rose to $15.9 million from $13.4 million. Nevertheless, EPS increased 40% YOY to $0.94, just above the consensus estimate of $0.93.

For Q3, Marvell guided EPS between $1.05 and $1.15. Gross margins for Q3 are expected to fall in the range of 57.5% to 58.5%.

Net cash from operating activities improved to $605.5 million from $461.6 million in the prior year. Overall, Marvell closed Q2 with $3.93 billion in cash and no short-term debt. Long-term debt of approximately $5 billion, however, continues to appear as higher interest expense on the income statement. Interest expense rose to $61.6 million from $51.9 million in the same period last year.

Meanwhile, the searing rally in MRVL stock this year has led to punchy valuations. Its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 56.1 times, price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 18.3 times, and price-to-cash flow (P/CF) multiple of 47.1 times are all above the sector medians of 21.1 times, 3.2 times, and 18.7 times, respectively.

What Do Analysts Think of MRVL Stock?

Taking all of this into account, analysts have a consensus "Strong Buy" rating for MRVL stock overall. Out of 39 analysts covering the stock, 28 have a "Strong Buy" rating, three have a "Moderate Buy" rating, and eight have a "Hold" rating. The mean target price of $317.05 denotes potential upside of 102% from current levels.

news.Title: Astera Labs Plunges 27% in 3 Months: Buy, Sell, or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Astera Labs ALAB shares have lost 26.7% in the past three months, underperforming the broader Zacks Computer & Technology sector and the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which declined 7.7% and 0.5%, respectively.

The company's shares have also underperformed its peers, which include Cisco Systems CSCO and Marvell Technology MRVL. Both companies are expanding their footprint in the AI infrastructure space. Shares of Cisco Systems and Marvell Technology have plunged 15.3% and 18.5%, respectively, in the past three-month period.

The underperformance can be attributed to rising operating expenses, increasing R&D investments and persistent supply constraints across the AI infrastructure industry.

However, ALAB's shares have outperformed its peers in the AI infrastructure space, including Credo Technology CRDO, which has lost 32.9% in the past three-month period. The outperformance can be attributed to its robust, diversified product portfolio that addresses growing demand for AI infrastructure and connectivity solutions, as well as its expanding customer base. Strong demand for its PCIe solutions has also been a major growth driver. These factors have help ALAB to fend off its competitors like Credo Technology.

ALAB Stock Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

ALAB Gains From Robust AI Connectivity Portfolio

Astera Labs is benefiting from robust demand for its AI connectivity solutions as hyperscalers accelerate investments in high-performance computing infrastructure. Its expanding portfolio of AI fabric switches, signal-conditioning products, memory controllers and optical connectivity solutions is strengthening its competitive position and supporting revenue growth. In the third quarter of 2026, revenues surged 153.7% year over year to $584.9 million.

The company's Scorpio AI fabric portfolio remains a major growth catalyst. In third-quarter 2026, Scorpio became its largest product family, surpassing $1 billion in annualized revenues. The high-volume ramp of Scorpio X-Series switches, alongside expanding adoption of P-Series products across hyperscaler platforms, is driving growth. Scorpio X-Series shipments expanded across multiple platforms, while additional customer engagements are expected to support momentum through 2027.

The company also benefits from increasing adoption of its Aries PCIe Gen 6 retimers and Taurus 400G and 800G connectivity solutions. The introduction of Aries 7, supporting next-generation PCIe Gen 7 copper and optical connectivity, further strengthens its competitive positioning.

The company's expanding portfolio of Leo smart memory controllers, optical connectivity solutions and Orion rack-scale architecture provides additional growth opportunities. Leo 2 products are expected to ramp in mid-2027, while Orion is projected to begin contributing revenues in 2027.

Story Continues

ALAB Offers Strong Q4 Guidance

Aster Labs is benefiting from strong demand for its expanding AI connectivity portfolio, which is expected to drive growth in the fourth quarter of 2026.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, revenues are expected to be between $730 million and $750 million. The midpoint implies approximately 27% sequential growth, driven by continued Scorpio X-Series and P-Series expansion, Aries PCIe 6 retimer demand and Taurus 800-gigabit deployments. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fourth-quarter revenues is pegged at $642 million, representing year-over-year growth of 137.27%.

Management projects non-GAAP earnings between $1.62 and $1.66 per share in the fourth quarter of 2026. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fourth-quarter 2026 earnings is pegged at $1.36 per share, which has been unchanged over the past 30 days. The figure implies a year-over-year increase of 134.48%.

Astera Labs, Inc. Price and Consensus

Astera Labs, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Astera Labs, Inc. Quote

ALAB Faces Rising Costs and Competitive Pressures

Despite ALAB's strong demand for its expanding AI connectivity portfolio, the company faced rising operating expenses in the third quarter of 2026, primarily due to increased investments in research and development, workforce expansion and higher variable compensation.

Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 19% sequentially to $162 million, reflecting higher spending on wafers, masks and intellectual property. Tight wafer capacity, power availability and memory supply across the AI infrastructure industry also posed challenges. Stiff competition from companies like Marvell Technology, Cisco Systems and Credo Technology also remains a concern.

ALAB Shares Trade at a Premium

Astera Labs' stock is trading at a premium, as suggested by the Value Score of F.

In terms of the forward 12-month Price/Sales, ALAB is trading at 14.23X, higher than the Computer & Technology sector's 5.01X.

ALAB Valuation

Conclusion

Astera Labs is well-positioned to benefit from strong AI infrastructure spending, supported by the rapid adoption of its Scorpio, Aries, Leo and Taurus product families. However, its stretched valuation, rising operating expenses and intensifying competition remain concerns.

Astera Labs currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), suggesting that it may be wise to wait for a more favorable entry point to accumulate the stock. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Credo Stock Dips 27% in the Past Month: What Should Investors Do Next?
news.Content:
Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd CRDO shares have plunged 26.6% over the past month compared with the Zacks Electronics-Semiconductors industry's decline of 20.1%, raising questions about whether the steep correction presents an attractive entry point or signals deeper concerns about the company's growth prospects.

Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The pullback is noteworthy given CRDO's position in the expanding artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure market. The rapid buildout of AI infrastructure is driving demand for its active electrical cables ("AEC"), optical solutions and retimers.

However, the expectations now seem demanding as the next leg of growth hinges on a sharp ramp in the optical business. For investors evaluating CRDO today, the investment debate goes beyond the headline numbers and centers on whether its expanding opportunity set is sufficient to offset the associated execution risks.

Robust Momentum Strengthens CRDO's Investment Case

As AI clusters grow larger, connectivity is emerging as a critical constraint. On the last earnings call, management highlighted that the challenge is no longer just bandwidth, but also reliability, power efficiency, signal integrity, telemetry and serviceability. Credo believes its system-level approach, which combines silicon, firmware, manufacturing tests and qualification, remains a key differentiator.

AEC is a system-level product for CRDO and its core growth engine. The company now has deep relationships with five hyperscalers, alongside expanding engagement with Neocloud customers. Credo continues to see higher AEC penetration within existing customers as deployments scale, while the shift toward 200-gig-per-lane 1.6T ports provides another growth opportunity.

The retimer business is another lucrative opportunity. Management noted that the retimer business also delivered record quarterly revenues, supported by scale-up deployments of Screaming Eagle at 100-gig-per-lane and initial contributions from its 200-gig-per-lane Blue Heron retimer.

The most significant shift in Credo's business mix is unfolding in its optical segment. On the last earnings call, management added that it continues to project more than $600 million in optical revenues, with ZeroFlap optics, silicon photonics PICs and optical DSPs each contributing over $100 million. Credo added that its optical DSP business generated "record revenues" in the fiscal first quarter. The company also recognized its first silicon-photonics PIC revenues following the DustPhotonics acquisition, with initial wins involving 800-gig and 1.6T optical transceivers. Credo continues to forecast more than 85% year-over-year revenue growth for fiscal 2027, aided by an expected second-half inflection.

The company's recent product announcements further strengthen its growth prospects. At the October 2026 OCP Global Summit, the company introduced its 1.6T ZeroFlap Active Light Cable ("ALC"). The wide-parallel optical interconnect solution is built for next-generation AI infrastructure, addressing rising reliability and energy-efficiency requirements. The solution targets AI scale-out and front-end networks, strengthening Credo's position in next-generation optical interconnects. Shipments are expected to begin in 2027.

Story Continues

Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd. Revenue (Quarterly)

Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd. revenue-quarterly | Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd. Quote

Alongside the new ALC, the company announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics Workstream within the Open Compute Project community. The initiative, backed by a leading hyperscaler and optical technology providers, including AFL, ams OSRAM and BizLink, aims to advance the development of the wide, parallel optical connectivity ecosystem.

The latest developments are built on the company's expanding product portfolio. In September 2026, Credo launched its new family of 224G-based ZF optical transceivers. The new products extend Credo's ZF architecture to 1.6T port speeds and combine its 224G-per-lane optical DSP with the Kfir200 silicon photonics-based PICs and latest-generation PILOT diagnostics platform.

The growth story becomes more compelling when viewed alongside improving profitability.

Non-GAAP gross margin reached 68%, while non-GAAP operating income totaled $230.6 million, producing an operating margin of 48.2% in the fiscal first quarter. Non-GAAP net income increased to $236.3 million, and the non-GAAP net margin was 49.3%.

Management expects fiscal 2027 non-GAAP gross margin to remain broadly consistent with fiscal 2026. It also expects non-GAAP net margin "to be in the vicinity" of 50%.

Although ALC and Omniconnect businesses remain at an early stage, they could diversify Credo's revenue base and create additional growth opportunities beyond traditional data-center interconnects.

Plenty of Challenges for CRDO

Despite the encouraging outlook, Credo faces risks that investors should not overlook.

Customer concentration remains significant. In the fiscal first quarter, four end customers generated roughly 84% of quarterly revenues. The four largest end customers represented 33%, 28%, 13% and 10% of revenues. Customer concentration is a major concern as it exposes the company to shifts in customer spending decisions and could materially affect results.

Execution risk is another risk factor. Much of the expected growth in fiscal 2027 is dependent on a successful ramp in the optical business. Any delay in deployment or broader industry transitions could affect this ramp.

Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd. Cash and Equivalents (Quarterly)

Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd. cash-equivalents-quarterly | Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd. Quote

Operating costs also warrant attention. Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 16% sequentially to $95.2 million during the fiscal first quarter, reflecting continued research and development investments. Management expects non-GAAP operating expenses to rise approximately 55% in fiscal 2027. Although this increase remains below anticipated revenue growth, higher spending could pressure profitability if sales expansion moderates.

Macroeconomic uncertainties and exposure to the AI investment cycle amid increasing market competition remain additional concerns. The DustPhotonics acquisition also reduced its cash, cash equivalents and short-term investment balance to $764.3 million at the end of the fiscal first quarter.

Competition from established players including Broadcom AVGO, Marvell Technology MRVL and Astera Labs ALAB across overlapping AI infrastructure markets may also impact CRDO's growth trajectory.

CRDO's Premium Valuation Leaves Little Room for Error

CRDO shares are trading at a forward price/earnings (P/E) multiple of 19.29X, higher than the industry's ratio of 9.08X.

The market is pricing in the explosive revenue momentum, strong profitability and expanding hyperscaler relationships. However, this leaves very little room for error. Any execution missteps or demand-supply chain troubles could lead to volatility in the stock.

Broadcom trades at a forward 12-month P/E multiple of 27.98X, while Astera Labs and Marvell are trading at a multiple of 39.86X and 26.05X, respectively.

Over the past month, shares of Broadcom, Astera Labs and Marvell are down 7.2%, 35.5% and 35.9%, respectively.

CRDO: What Should Investors Do Next?

The fundamental outlook remains encouraging. The expanding portfolio of optical DSPs, silicon-photonics PICs, ZeroFlap Optics, retimers, ALCs and OmniConnect could steadily broaden Credo's addressable market and reduce its dependence on a single product category over time.

However, customer concentration, increasing expenses and the need to execute a substantial second-half optical ramp leave little room for disappointment.

For existing shareholders, holding Credo's seems prudent given strong operating momentum and expanding AI connectivity opportunity. However, new investors may benefit from a more attractive entry point rather than aggressively buying the dip.

At present, CRDO carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here

news.Title: Marvell's Deal to Acquire Lumentum Could Be a Game Changer for the Stock
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) has been a big winner this year, with the stock up more than 130% in 2026, as of the end of October. However, an announced deal to acquire Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE) could be a game changer for what has already been a good story.

This deal is all about optical networking, as it will combine Marvell's leadership in optical interconnects with Lumentum's strength in lasers. Marvell called the deal a "once-in-a-generation opportunity to define and lead AI connectivity in the era of integrated optics," as it will provide the company with end-to-end design capabilities that will allow it to accelerate its time to market and solve the increasing complexity of scale-up and scale-out networks.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Let's see what this could all mean for investors.

Complementary technologies

The two companies' optics technologies are very complementary. In an optical network, Marvell provides electronic components such as DSPs (digital signal processors) that prepare data to be converted into optical signals; transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs) that convert light signals back into electrical signals; and silicon photonics (SiPho) engines that combine hundreds of components to improve the performance and energy efficiency of optical interconnects.

Lumentum produces high-power indium phosphide (InP) lasers and gallium arsenide (GaAs) vertical cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) that convert electricity into light for high-speed data transmission. It is one of a handful of companies with this technology for these advanced lasers. Designing and manufacturing these lasers is a complex task, and the company holds over 1,000 patents and owns specialized semiconductor fabs (manufacturing facilities).

Marvell said that the acquisition will allow it to go from producing components to full modules. It will also create meaningful design and operational efficiencies for its customers. It believes that integrating its technology with Lumentum is ultimately needed to take bandwidth, latency, and power efficiency to the next level.

The deal will combine what are expected to be two of the S&P 500 's fastest-growing companies by earnings per share (EPS) from 2026 through 2028. Meanwhile, Marvell believes its combined total addressable market (TAM) will be around $550 billion by 2030. It sees $1 billion in potential annual synergies with the deal, largely coming from a reduction in cost of goods sold. Excluding synergies, the company will have a $17.7 billion annual revenue run rate with 57% gross margins and 39% operating margins .

Story Continues

As part of the deal, Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they own. The deal valued Lumentum at an enterprise value of $115 billion, or about $1,132 per share, at the time of the announcement. That represents about a 24% premium to its closing price before the announcement. The deal is expected to close in the first half of calendar 2028.

Time to buy the stocks

Both Marvell and Lumentum have been riding the shift in AI data centers from copper wire to optical networks, which offer better bandwidth and lower energy costs. As AI innovation continues to advance and systems become more powerful, the need for optical networking should only grow.

Both companies are already seeing strong growth individually. Lumentum reported its fiscal first-quarter results the same day as the merger announcement. It grew its revenue by 137% to $1.26 billion, while its gross margins climbed 1,700 basis points to 51%. Meanwhile, Marvell had guided for its current quarter revenue to increase by 52%, with data center revenue surging 75%. The combined company will become a juggernaut in the optical space.

Marvell is more than optics, though, as it is also a leader in custom AI chips. It provides important IP (intellectual property) for both Amazon 's AI Trainium chips and Microsoft 's newer Maia chips. It also recently won a deal to supply Alphabet 's Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) architecture with important attach components, such as inference accelerators, storage controllers, NICs, memory interface controllers, and near-memory compute.

Marvell's pending acquisition of Lumentum, plus its strength in custom AI chips, gives Marvell one of the best long-term growth outlooks in the AI infrastructure space. That makes the AI stock a buy, with Lumentum being a discounted way to own Marvell -- although there is always some risk that a deal may not go through.

news.Title: Marvell Stock Has Plunged 46% Since Jensen Huang Called It the Next $1 Trillion Company. Here's Why.
news.Content:
In early June, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang called Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) the next trillion-dollar company. Huang explained that Marvell's connectivity solutions are essential for coordinating large clusters of processors powering artificial intelligence (AI) systems.

Wall Street initially embraced this optimism. Marvell shares surged to about $291 on June 2 and reached a record closing price of nearly $316 just two days later. However, enthusiasm around Marvell seems to have evaporated. As of Nov. 2, Marvell stock traded at $171, representing a decline of 46% from its peak.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

MRVL data by YCharts

The sell-off follows Marvell's announcement that it is acquiring optical networking specialist Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE) in a $115 billion deal . Let's unpack why Wall Street is reacting so negatively to this news and assess whether investors are overlooking the long-term opportunity.

Why Jensen Huang sees trillion-dollar potential in Marvell

Marvell is quietly becoming an important supplier to the AI infrastructure supercycle. The company's custom application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) allow hyperscalers to build processors optimized for particular training and inference workloads, while its networking and connectivity products help transfer information between chips and servers.

Nvidia recognized this opportunity early on, announcing a $2 billion investment in Marvell and a partnership involving its NVLink Fusion platform. The collaboration allows AI developers to combine custom silicon designed by Marvell with Nvidia's broader computing and networking architectures.

Why the Lumentum acquisition sent Marvell stock plunging

On Nov. 2, Marvell announced an agreement to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction carrying an implied enterprise value of approximately $115 billion. The acquisition values Lumentum at approximately $1,132 per share, representing a 24% premium to its closing price on Oct. 28, right as speculation about the deal surfaced.

The transaction's structure is important to understand. Rather than paying cash or taking on debt to finance the acquisition, Marvell will issue 4.5 new shares for every outstanding Lumentum share. Following the transaction, Marvell shareholders will own 67% of the combined company while Lumentum shareholders will control the remaining 33%.

Story Continues

This means Marvell's investors are effectively surrendering one-third of the combined company's ownership to acquire Lumentum. That dilution explains Wall Street's negative reaction. However, since the agreement uses a fixed exchange ratio rather than a guaranteed cash price, the value Lumentum shareholders ultimately receive will fluctuate with Marvell's stock price. In other words, the acquisition's headline valuation isn't necessarily the price Marvell will actually pay.

Is Wall Street overlooking Marvell's long-term potential?

Despite the dilution, I think there are some meaningful benefits to this deal. Marvell's portfolio includes digital signal processors (DSPs), networking chips, and connectivity solutions that enable data to move through AI systems. Lumentum complements those capabilities with lasers and optical components used to transmit information at low latencies. Combining these solutions allows Marvell to offer customers a more complete optical connectivity suite.

Management expects the transaction to generate more than $1 billion in annual run rate cost synergies and become accretive to adjusted earnings per share (EPS) during the first year post-close.

Although the market's reaction has been severe so far, investors should not lose sight of Marvell's long-term potential. During its investor day last month, management estimated that its total addressable market (TAM) could reach $400 billion by calendar 2030. Following the proposed Lumentum acquisition, the combined company's addressable market is expected to expand to $550 billion.

Another important development involves Alphabet . In August, Marvell disclosed an agreement to develop custom semiconductors supporting Google's Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) ecosystem. As part of the arrangement, Google received warrants to purchase 59 million Marvell shares at $206.58 each.

I think the agreements with Google and Nvidia reinforce Marvell's rising position as an important partner to some of the world's largest AI infrastructure customers. Ultimately, Marvell's acquisition of Lumentum could strengthen its competitive position by bridging optical components and semiconductor design under one roof.

Nevertheless, the market seems to be focusing on what existing shareholders need to give up in the short term. Huang's trillion-dollar prediction remains ambitious, but the strategic rationale behind his enthusiasm hasn't disappeared just because Marvell's stock price is falling.

For investors willing to tolerate volatility in the near term and wait a few years for the acquisition's benefits to materialize in both revenue and profit, Marvell's sell-off could represent an attractive opportunity to buy the dip.
