news.Title: Micron Stock Jumps 36% in Six Months: Is There More Upside Ahead?
news.Content:
Micron Technology, Inc. MU has delivered an impressive 35.9% gain over the past six months, even as macroeconomic uncertainty and geopolitical tensions have weighed on the broader market. The stock has comfortably outperformed the Zacks Computer and Technology sector, which has declined 3.9% during the same period.

Micron has also outpaced several prominent semiconductor stocks, including Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN, NVIDIA Corporation NVDA and Marvell Technology, Inc. MRVL. Shares of Texas Instruments, NVIDIA and Marvell Technology have gained 12.1%, 6.7% and 3.1%, respectively, over the past six months.

Micron Six-Month Price Return Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The strong rally reflects Micron's growing importance in the artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem. The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is creating enormous demand for advanced memory chips, particularly high-bandwidth memory (HBM), DRAM and data center solid-state drives (SSDs). With these trends expected to support industry growth for several years, Micron appears well-positioned to benefit.

However, after such a sharp rally, investors may wonder whether the stock still offers an attractive entry point. A closer look at its financial performance, growth opportunities and valuation suggests that Micron's rally may still have room to run.

Micron's Financial Performance Continues to Impress

Micron's fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results highlight the strength of its current business momentum. The company reported revenues of $54.23 billion, soaring 379% year over year. This marked its sixth consecutive quarterly revenue record.

The bottom line was equally impressive. Non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) surged to $33.42 from $3.03 in the year-ago quarter. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded significantly to 87% from 45.7%, reflecting strong pricing conditions and a favorable product mix.

Micron Technology, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Micron Technology, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Micron Technology, Inc. Quote

Micron's cash generation also improved considerably. Operating cash flow reached nearly $44 billion in the fourth quarter, taking the full fiscal 2026 figure to $89.68 billion.

Management expects this momentum to continue. For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Micron projects revenues of $61.5 billion, plus or minus $1.5 billion, and non-GAAP EPS of $38.15, plus or minus $1. These estimates indicate year-over-year growth of approximately 351% in revenues and 698% in earnings.

Story Continues

Such guidance reinforces the view that Micron is operating in an exceptionally strong memory market. While quarterly growth rates of this magnitude may eventually moderate, the company's earnings outlook remains encouraging.

AI Spending Creates a Long Growth Runway for Micron

AI remains the biggest growth opportunity for Micron. Modern AI systems require significantly more memory bandwidth and capacity than traditional computing systems. Training and running increasingly complex AI models require advanced memory solutions, particularly HBM, high-performance DRAM and data center SSDs.

The capital spending plans of major cloud companies strengthen this opportunity. Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta Platforms are expected to invest nearly $745 billion in capital expenditures in 2026, with a substantial portion directed toward AI infrastructure.

This spending is important for Micron because AI servers require considerably more memory than conventional servers. As AI models become larger and workloads more complex, memory content per server is likely to increase. This should support demand for Micron's advanced memory products.

Micron's HBM business is already benefiting from this trend. HBM revenues grew faster than total company revenues in the fourth quarter. The company has also secured agreements for most of its 2027 HBM bit supply at significantly higher prices than the previous year. Micron is progressing with its HBM4 production ramp-up and working with NVIDIA on a custom HBM4E solution. These developments could strengthen its position in the high-end AI memory market.

NAND storage is emerging as another important growth driver. Micron's data center SSD revenues came in at $10 billion in the fourth quarter, more than 10 times the year-ago level. Increasing AI workloads and applications such as KV-cache offload are creating additional demand for high-performance storage solutions.

Beyond data centers, physical AI could open another growth avenue. Autonomous vehicles and humanoid robots are expected to require substantially more memory and storage than today's systems. Although this opportunity may take time to develop, it could provide another source of demand later this decade.

Long-Term SCAs Improve Revenue Visibility for Micron

Apart from strong AI demand, Micron is taking steps to make its business more predictable. The company has signed 26 Strategic Customer Agreements (SCAs), which it expects to cover more than 35% of its revenues through 2030. Financial commitments from customers under these agreements have increased to $32 billion, with most of the amount backed by cash deposits.

These take-or-pay agreements are important because they provide Micron with better visibility into future demand and help the company plan its manufacturing capacity more efficiently. They also strengthen relationships with major customers and support long-term technology collaboration.

Micron is also investing heavily to expand its manufacturing and packaging capabilities across the United States, Singapore, Japan and Taiwan. Its ID1 fabrication facility is expected to begin wafer output in mid-2027, while its Singapore HBM packaging facility is expected to start initial production in early 2027. These investments should help Micron address growing demand and strengthen its position in advanced memory manufacturing.

Micron's Valuation Still Looks Attractive

Despite its impressive rally, Micron's valuation remains relatively low. The stock currently trades at a forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of just 4.65, significantly below the sector average of 17.09.

Micron Forward 12-Month P/E Ratio

Micron also looks inexpensive compared with several semiconductor peers. Texas Instruments, Marvell Technology and NVIDIA trade at a forward P/E multiple of 29.02, 26.05 and 14.57, respectively.

This valuation gap is particularly interesting, given Micron's exceptional earnings growth and strong position in the AI memory market.

Final Thoughts: Micron Stock Still Worth Buying

Micron's 35.9% rally over the past six months reflects a significant improvement in its business fundamentals. Strong AI-related memory demand, rising HBM revenues, favorable pricing conditions and robust cash generation have transformed its earnings outlook.

The company's long-term customer agreements also provide better revenue visibility, while investments in manufacturing and packaging capacity should help it capture future demand.

Micron's growth prospects remain compelling, and its valuation looks attractive relative to its earnings potential and semiconductor peers. Given the strong demand outlook and improving fundamentals, investors should consider buying MU stock at current levels for long-term gains.

Micron currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

news.Title: MRVL Plunges 36% in a Month: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology MRVL shares have lost 35.9% in the past month compared with the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry and the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's decline of 22% and 14.1%, respectively.

MRVL One-Month Performance Chart

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Despite the downward movement in MRVL's stock price, MRVL has remained at a premium valuation. MRVL stock is trading at a P/S multiple of 8.58X, much higher than the industry's multiple of 3.08X. The premium valuation is further substantiated by a Zacks Value Score of F.

MRVL Forward 12-Month (P/S) Valuation Chart

Given the dynamics, investors must be wondering if it's the right time to invest, retain or sell the stock. Let's discuss the fundamentals of the company to get a better insight.

MRVL Stock Faces a Temporary Setback Amid Long-Term AI Growth

The decline in MRVL's stock price has come amid a broader sell-off in AI-related stocks spanning hyperscalers, semiconductor companies and AI infrastructure providers, as investors increasingly question whether massive AI investments will generate sufficient returns. Since MRVL supplies its solutions to these infrastructure providers, MRVL's stock has also been affected.

Marvell's recent stock decline coincides with the announcement of its proposed $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum Holdings LITE. Under the terms of the all-stock deal, Lumentum stockholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of 4.5 shares of Marvell common stock for each Lumentum share held, raising investor concerns over valuation, shareholder dilution and the transaction's potential impact on earnings.

However, in the long term, the acquisition of Lumentum will add a substantial portfolio of optical and photonic technologies used in AI data centers, cloud infrastructure, telecommunications networks and advanced manufacturing. Lumentum's Optical Circuit Switching, high-speed transceivers and laser components are of the most strategic importance for MRVL.

Marvell's accelerating AI-driven growth provides a favorable backdrop for its proposed acquisition of Lumentum. Marvell's second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues increased 37% year over year to $2.74 billion, led by a 46% increase in data-center revenues to $2.17 billion, which accounted for 79% of total sales. Management raised its fiscal 2027 revenue growth outlook to approximately 45%, or roughly $12 billion, while expecting data-center revenues to increase about 60%, up from its prior expectation of approximately 50%.

Story Continues

Within Marvell's portfolio, custom silicon is emerging as an increasingly important growth driver as hyperscalers expand their demand for specialized XPUs and XPU-attach products. AI connectivity also remains strong, with demand for 800G optical DSPs continuing and 1.6T products ramping rapidly. Marvell's scale-out switching business is on track to more than double in fiscal 2027, driven by growing adoption of 51.2T switches across a broader customer base. Meanwhile, increasing customer interest in scale-up optics and switching solutions could provide additional growth opportunities as AI infrastructure architectures evolve.

MRVL to Benefit From a Broader Portfolio

The integration of MRVL's electrical and optical interconnect, switching and custom silicon technologies with Lumentum's high-performance lasers, optical transceivers and optical circuit switching capabilities is expected to create a comprehensive connectivity portfolio spanning scale-across, scale-out, scale-up and scale-in architectures. These factors will strengthen MRVL's competitive positioning relative to Broadcom AVGO and enhance its ability to compete with Coherent COHR.

Broadcom is a leader in the domain of custom silicon solutions for data centers. Broadcom's advanced 3.5D XDSiP packaging platform is critical to ensure the performance and efficiency of custom AI XPUs. Combining Marvell's custom silicon, switching and DSP technologies with Lumentum's lasers, transceivers and optical switching could help MRVL compete with Broadcom's integrated AI connectivity portfolio.

Coherent is a vertically integrated manufacturer of lasers, transceivers, optoelectronic devices and modules and engineered materials that serve communications, industrial, instrumentation and electronics markets. Lumentum's optical components and laser technologies would strengthen MRVL's optical portfolio, enabling it to compete more effectively with Coherent in high-performance lasers and optical connectivity.

Amid these developments, investors need to keep a close eye on Marvell's ability to translate the acquisition of Lumentum into meaningful competitive gains. MRVL's profitability remains sensitive to product mix as newer data center platforms ramp up. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MRVL's fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $4.21 per share, implying year-over-year growth of 48%. Estimates have remained unchanged for the past 30 days.

Conclusion

The recent decline in Marvell's stock price may present an opportunity for investors seeking exposure to the expanding AI infrastructure market. MRVL's strengths in custom silicon, optical connectivity, switching and data-center interconnect, along with its proposed acquisition of Lumentum, could support its long-term growth prospects.

However, the proposed acquisition also introduces integration, shareholder dilution and execution risks. Investors should closely monitor the transaction's progress, MRVL's profitability trends and the company's ability to translate its expanding portfolio into sustainable earnings growth.

Currently, MRVL stock carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: QQQ, CoreWeave, SanDisk, Marvell, Arm and Micron
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 4, 2026– Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Nasdaq 100 Index QQQ, CoreWeave CRWV, SanDisk SNDK, Marvell MRVL, Arm Holdings ARM and Micron MU.

Q4 QQQ Roadmap: Navigating AI Turbulence & Market Headwinds

2026 Stock Market Review

Here is a roadmap of what has occurred with the Nasdaq 100 Index in 2026.

Overall, there are 3 major takeaways:

1)      The market continues to climb the proverbial wall of worry. If I had told you oil and rates are where they are, and the market has held up this well, few would have believed me.

2)      The market and the economy depend heavily AI. The slightest concern of AI infrastructure spending slowing sends stocks crashing.

3)      Market indices don't tell the full story.

Tech Destruction

Last year, investors complained that tech was holding up the market; now the narrative has flipped. QQQ just suffered its worst 3-day decline since "Liberation Day." Meanwhile, according to Morgan Stanley, U.S. tech momentum, or the lack of it, has been worse than the dot-com bust.

What is Holding Back the Equity Market?

· Inflation/Higher Interest Rates

· AI Political Headwinds

· AI Funding/Debt Fears

· Gravity/Profit Taking

Below I explain why the market will overcome these hurdles in the coming months:

Inflation & Higher Rates

Higher energy prices have led to inflation concerns and higher interest rates. That said, geopolitical energy shocks are often short-lived. Tuesday, energy prices fell sharply after Al-Araby Al-Jadeed reported progress toward a US–Iran agreement involving nuclear concessions and frozen funds.

The latest projections lean heavily toward 3 to 4 rate hikes (25 bps increments) over the path extending into mid-to-late 2027. According to BlueKurtic Market Insights (@BlueKurtic), the data shows that equities can perform well during rate-hiking cycles, especially if the pace is measured. This looks like a non-cyclical hike, with no more than 2-3 hikes. This scenario usually hasn't been bad for stocks. The last non-cyclical hike was in 1997, and the S&P 500 gained 40% over the next year, outperforming longer hiking cycles.

Midterm Election Impact: Gridlock is Good

According to a Reuters Poll, only a third of Americans approve of the fast pace of data-center construction. In my view, the stock market has been pricing in a Democratic "Blue Wave" for a few months now, and that is part of why we have seen carnage in AI stocks. Nevertheless, the stock market during periods of divided government has "typically exceeded returns achieved when one political party controls the White House, Senate, and House of Representatives."

Story Continues

The stock market has been pricing in a "Blue Wave" for a few months now, and that is part of the reasons we have seen carnage in AI stocks. In other words, because the market is a forward discounting mechanism, I believe it will result in a classic "sell the rumor, buy the news" situation. Seasonality data backs this notion up. The S&P 500 has finished higher in the six months following every midterm election since 1950. That's 19 consecutive elections with an average gain of nearly 15% regardless of which party came out on top.

AI Debt/Funding Fears

CoreWeave shares plunged in October after its bond yields jumped to distressed levels. Although CoreWeave is plagued by high-debt levels, the market has been acting as if it will go bankrupt. However, betting markets suggest that won't happen any time soon. In September, PolyMarket priced a 2027 CoreWeave bankruptcy as high as 50%. Today, that number is just 12%.

Tech Stock Gravity & Profit Taking

Earlier this year, many AI-related names went too far, too fast. For example, SanDisk blew past the 4.236% bull flag Fibonacci extension by a lot (highly unusual and very rare) and jumped 4,000% in a year. Also, shares were 264% above the 200-day. Typically, a stock 200% above the 200-day is very extreme. In other words, AI stocks got too far ahead of themselves. I think of the 200-day MA as a bungee cord. If it gets too far, it pulls you back in. However, even the strongest stocks retreat to the 200-day. Now, I believe it has overshot. The first touch is often a fantastic area. We are seeing this across many AI stocks including, Marvell , Arm Holdings , Micron and many others.

Bottom Line

While headline fears around AI leverage, interest rates, and political shifts have triggered sharp sector rotation, the market's technical foundation remains intact. Extended growth leaders are completing necessary mean-reversion pullbacks to major moving averages, clearing out leverage while forward-looking indicators point to a classic post-midterm rally. As historical seasonality and political gridlock align with favorable risk-reward entries across core infrastructure names, the current pullback presents a compelling backdrop for the next leg higher.

Research Chief Names "Single Best Pick to Double"

From thousands of stocks, 5 Zacks experts each have chosen their favorite to skyrocket +100% or more in months to come. From those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian hand-picks one to have the most explosive upside of all.

This company targets millennial and Gen Z audiences, generating nearly $1 billion in revenue last quarter alone. A recent pullback makes now an ideal time to jump aboard. Of course, all our elite picks aren't winners but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks' Stocks Set to Double like Nano-X Imaging which shot up +129.6% in little more than 9 months.

news.Title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Lilly, Cisco, KLA, Oil-Dri Corp. of America and NVE
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 4, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: Lilly and Co. LLY, Cisco Systems, Inc. CSCO, KLA Corp. KLAC, Oil-Dri Corp. of America ODC and NVE Corp. NVEC.

Here are highlights from Tuesday's Analyst Blog:

Top Analyst Reports for Eli Lilly, Cisco and KLA

The Zacks Research Daily presents the best research output of our analyst team. Today's Research Daily features new research reports on 16 major stocks, including Eli Lilly and Co., Cisco Systems, Inc. and KLA Corp., as well as two micro-cap stocks Oil-Dri Corp. of America and NVE Corp.. The Zacks microcap research is unique as our research content on these small and under-the-radar companies is the only research of its type in the country.

These research reports have been hand-picked from the roughly 70 reports published by our analyst team today.

You can see all of today's research reports here >>>

Today's Featured Research Reports

Eli Lilly's shares have outperformed the Zacks Large Cap Pharmaceuticals industry over the year-to-date period (+31.9% vs. +26.2%). The company's Q3 earnings and sales beat estimates. Demand for its popular GLP-1 drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, remains strong, making them the company's key top-line drivers.

Lilly's other new drugs like Kisunla, Omvoh and Jaypirca are also contributing to top-line growth. It is also making rapid pipeline progress in obesity and diabetes. Its new oral GLP-1 obesity pill, Foundayo, is expected to be a commercial game-changer. Its next-generation weight loss pill, retatrutide, if approved, could become another multibillion-dollar product.

Over the past couple of years, Lilly has announced several M&A deals aimed at diversifying beyond GLP-1 drugs and expanding its presence in immunology, oncology and neuroscience. Rising pricing pressure on some drugs and potential competition in the GLP-1 market are some top-line headwinds.

(You can read the full research report on Eli Lilly here >>> )

Shares of Cisco have outperformed the Zacks Computer - Networking industry over the year-to-date period (+34.3% vs. +33.7%). The company's prospects are benefiting from broad demand across networking, security and collaboration. AI infrastructure orders, integrated silicon and an end-of-support refresh opportunity support a multi-year networking cycle, while newer security products and Splunk's recovery broaden the growth base.

Cisco also retains operating leverage and continues to return cash to shareholders. Offsetting these positives, a hardware-led revenue mix is expected to limit gross-margin expansion, while services recovery should remain gradual. Competition across networking and security still requires sustained product execution.

news.Title: 華邦電賺翻股價卻跌停？  專家喊「派對未結束」 大摩最新目標價出爐
news.Content:
記憶體大廠華邦電（2344）近日公布第三季財，EPS高達7.58元，前三季累計 15.32元，毛利率更衝上70.6%，不過股民並未買單，華邦電3日股價連慘遭打入跌停，今（4）日更是觸及132.5元波段新低，連兩日累積跌幅超過16%。

對此，投資專家「股人阿勳」分析，市場不買單的理由是「記憶體漲價太兇」，就連蘋果都開始承受不了成本壓力，必須透過調漲產品售價轉嫁消費者，一旦終端需求受到影響，上游記憶體的拉貨動能自然可能放緩。

股人阿勳補充，雖然這個擔憂有道理，但現在宣布派對結束恐怕還太早，畢竟華邦電也在法說提到，記憶體供給仍然吃緊，甚至預期2027年可能比今年更缺貨。

不過值得一提的是，華邦電第三季獲利暴增，很大一部分來自記憶體價格上漲，而不是出貨量同步暴增。股人阿勳認為，這代表未來即使記憶體價格沒有下跌，只要漲價速度放緩，獲利成長就可能跟著降溫。「投資景氣循環股最怕什麼？不是公司開始虧錢，而是公司還在大賺特賺，股價卻已經提前反映下一輪景氣下滑。」

股人阿勳直言，比起華邦電今年能賺多少，所以他更在意的是，在目前這麼好的獲利下，明、後年還能維持多少？「派對不一定結束，但當所有人都覺得酒喝不完的時候，反而要開始注意誰準備買單了！」

此外，大摩在最新的研究報告中指出，華邦電毛利率來到70.6%，大幅高於大摩預估12.5個百分點；管理層預計第4季將持續成長，但隨著非AI需求趨緩，成長力道也有所收斂。

產能規劃部分，大摩預期高雄廠Module A 2026年底前達到每月2.4 萬至2.5萬片、16nm製程將從約2000片擴至1.6萬片，足以支撐2027年下半年的出貨需求，因此將華邦電的目標價調升至288元，並給予「優於大盤」的評等。

（封面示意圖／翻攝Pexels）

news.Title: 5 tech stock stalwarts have tumbled over 50%
news.Content: The technology boom version 2.0 has been driven by insatiable spending on data center infrastructure. That spending continues, but many of the companies providing the hardware necessary to run AI chatbots, like ChatGPT and Gemini, are in the midst of a brutal sell-off that's knocked the technology-heavy Nasdaq 100 down nearly 10% and flirting with correction territory. The pain has been particularly hard felt among semiconductors and cloud plays, many of which have been taken to the proverbial woodshed, including these five, which tumbled over 50% from summertime highs to recent lows: Intel: -58% Arm Holdings: -55% Oracle: -52% Sandisk: -53% KLA Corporation: -52% Source: Yahoo! Historical Quotes AI spending boom fears take root Stocks tend to move based on emotion, and now, into its fourth year, the AI trade has gotten pretty crowded. I've seen this movie before during my 30-year career, so it's not surprising to me to see the drawdowns. The usual progression: A new idea lands with many doubters and few believers. As stocks run, more converts jump on board until most of the money on the sidelines has joined the party, leaving few new buyers to step in to support stocks on pullbacks. Tech stocks like Intel didn't drop because their businesses have suddenly imploded. Instead, they've dropped because supply from sellers locking in gains has dwarfed demand. Basic economics sounds simplistic, but sometimes the simple answer is the correct one. If there's a specific catalyst beyond protecting gains, ratcheting back peak data-center spending is the most compelling. There's mounting fear that we're about to hit peak capex for data center spending in 2027, setting the stage for a slowdown. The stakes are high, given the dollars at stake. In mid-October, JPMorgan said 2026 AI capex for the five biggest hyperscalers (Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle, and Microsoft) would be $900 billion, climbing above $1 trillion in 2027. More Tech: Meta and Microsoft just sent employees a memo about Anthropic Microsoft cutting off popular software with no extension Oct. 13 Apple's biggest AI advantage may face new privacy challenge Most of that spending to date has been financed by free cash flow (and, arguably, by circular financing deals, thanks to investments from the likes of Nvidia). However, companies are increasingly turning to debt, exposing balance sheets to risk. For instance, Goldman Sachs pegged the percentage of AI capex financed by debt at 33% in 2026, up from 26% in 2025. In 2027, Goldman Sachs says 35% will be paid for by debt, totaling roughly $400 billion. Story Continues If revenue growth underdelivers or lenders get antsy and borrowing gets pricier, we could end up with a major capex reset that unravels the AI trade, or so the bear argument goes. Bank of America says demand justifies spending There's a silver lining to more judicious AI capex, though, suggests Bank of America. Analyst Vivek Arya thinks that if capex budget cuts happen, it would "lower peak profit but preserve compute scarcity, extend the AI cycle and support higher multiples over time." Think a shorter peak and a flatter runway for the entire AI cycle, which could mean less boom-and-bust action for underlying stocks. Arya thinks there's plenty of incentive to continue investing in AI, given surging backlogs. "With $2.5tn+ backlog and surging enterprise adoption, demand looks durable: scarce compute, not excess capacity, is the risk," wrote Arya in a research note shared with me. Also read : Elon Musk sends incredible news to Micron stock investors "Slower supply growth against resilient demand could lift utilization, support pricing and reduce overbuild risk. The result could be lower peak earnings, but a longer earnings runway and potentially higher multiples for chipmakers already valued as if the cycle is ending," added Arya. Major hyperscaler revenue certainly seems to support the argument for spending. Amazon's AWS revenue rose 39%, Microsoft Azure sales grew 49%, and Google AI revenue increased over 100% year over year in the third quarter, according to Arya. Are beat-down tech stocks bargain bin buys? The risk of a slowdown or debt reckoning is reflected in the most punished technology stocks. Intel has been late to the party in terms of AI-optimized chips, but optimism over U.S. fab capacity builds, and deeper pockets from U.S. and Nvidia investments caused its shares to soar before the recent drop, despite operational headwinds. At Oracle, the fear of overspending to become one of the biggest hyperscalers has raised major debt concerns, contributing to its recent drop, despite the company's argument that its backlog is solid and justifies the push. ARM Holdings makes its money by selling semiconductor designs, and a slowdown in data center spending would crimp its upside. It has historically traded at a premium valuation because of its 'asset-light/no-fab' status, making it more susceptible to drawdowns as investors press sell on so-called expensive players first. A downthrottling in capex would also be bad news for KLA Corporation, which makes inspection and measurement machines used to create semiconductors. If the data center buildout slows, so would chip demand, and the need for new fab equipment. Like ARM, KLA has long been considered a premium play in the semiconductor equipment space, trading at a higher valuation than peers such as Applied Materials and Lam Research, making it susceptible to sell-offs. SanDisk sits in a different space, given that it makes memory, but lower spending on high-end server capacity means less memory is needed. Given the 303% surge in NAND flash memory this past year, and the historical cyclical nature of memory market demand, a bit of investors' caution is warranted. It's hard to judge whether any of these individual stock drawdowns have run their course and are ready to reverse, but Arya thinks semiconductor plays aren't overpriced relative to history. "Since CY19, the SOX index has traded at 12.5x-30x forward PE multiple, ranging from a 20% discount to a 40% premium versus SPX. Today, 16.4x represents a 10% discount, consistent with AI-cycle troughs in CY23-1H26 and only 10pts above the deepest relative discount since CY19." Of course, stocks can always get cheaper, but Arya's math shows that these stocks aren't historically priced excessively, and that should give some modicum of comfort to bargain hunters, especially if Arya is right that a capex reset wouldn't trigger demand destruction nearly to the extent some fear. "The market therefore appears to be discounting capex risk before the demand data have cracked. If paying AI demand stays resilient, lower capex could reduce overbuild, preserve scarcity, extend the EPS cycle and justify higher multiples, in our opinion," concluded Arya. news.Title: What Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) Said on Its Q4 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Skyworks Solutions, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Skyworks closed its Qorvo acquisition after its fiscal Q4 ended, so reported quarterly results cover legacy Skyworks only; its December-quarter outlook is for the combined company. Q4 revenue was $1.046 billion and non-GAAP EPS was $1.28, both slightly above guidance midpoints.

The combined company expects December-quarter revenue of $1.8 billion to $1.9 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.25 at the midpoint. Smartphone revenue is expected to decline sequentially, while Diversified Growth Markets—including data center, defense and automotive—are expected to grow.

Skyworks reiterated a target of at least $500 million in annual cost synergies from the deal, with most earnings benefits expected in the second half of fiscal 2027. Longer-term targets include mid- to high-single-digit revenue growth and 50% to 55% gross margins within 24 to 36 months.

Apple Cut iPhone 18 Orders; What Does It Mean For Suppliers?

Skyworks Solutions (NASDAQ:SWKS) reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results as a standalone company and outlined its first outlook as a combined business following the October 5 closing of its acquisition of Qorvo.

Chief Executive Officer and President Phil Brace said the combination brings greater scale, a broader technology portfolio and an expanded manufacturing footprint. The company will report its operations going forward in two categories: smartphone and Diversified Growth Markets.

→ LyondellBasell's Dividend Looks Safer, But a New Risk Could Change That

MarketBeat Week in Review – 06/23 - 6/27

Because the Qorvo transaction closed after Skyworks' fiscal fourth-quarter end, Skyworks' September-quarter results reflect only the legacy Skyworks business, while December-quarter guidance is on a combined-company basis.

Fourth-Quarter Results and Market Trends

For the fiscal quarter ended October 2, Skyworks reported revenue of $1.046 billion, above the midpoint of its guidance range of $1.035 billion. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share were $1.28, $0.01 above the midpoint of guidance.

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

Skyworks Stock Down 16% in 2025, Poised for AI Edge Surge

Gross profit was $465 million, representing a gross margin of 44.4%, while operating expenses totaled $237 million. Operating income was $227 million, or 21.7% of revenue. Net income was $193 million. Skyworks ended the quarter with approximately $2.6 billion in cash and investments and roughly $2.5 billion in debt, including acquisition financing completed ahead of the Qorvo closing.

Story Continues

The company repurchased $107 million of stock during the quarter at an average price of $66.27 per share.

→ Exxon's Refining Profits Soared—Did Chevron Get the Same Windfall?

Mobile represented about 60% of Skyworks' standalone quarterly revenue, supported by demand from its largest customer during the company's seasonally strongest period. Brace said this was partly offset by continued weakness in Android, where Skyworks is concentrating on the premium tier.

Broad markets represented approximately 40% of revenue and grew 9% year over year in the quarter and about 10% for fiscal 2026. The company cited data center, Wi-Fi and automotive as growth drivers, while consumer IoT remained soft. Skyworks' largest customer accounted for approximately 62% of quarterly revenue, including non-smartphone products.

Brace said demand and book-to-bill trends were healthy across end markets, while timing and power products continued to gain design engagement in AI data centers. He also said automotive and industrial design activity was robust. However, management said higher input costs remain a margin headwind and are expected to persist. The company is responding through factory-load optimization, long-term supply agreements and price increases where appropriate.

Combined Business Structure and Growth Markets

On a pro forma combined basis, Skyworks said fiscal 2026 smartphone revenue was approximately $4.6 billion, down about 11% from the prior year. Management attributed the decline to expected Android weakness and content dynamics at its largest customer.

Brace said the combined company now offers a full RF front-end platform for next-generation smartphones and intends to focus investments on premium devices, where RF content is higher. He said 5G Advanced and 6G could add RF complexity through additional transmit and receive paths, spectrum bands, satellite connectivity, filters, amplifiers and antenna solutions.

Management expects the broader product portfolio to reduce reliance on individual sockets and help create steadier smartphone results. Brace characterized smartphone as a long-term low-single-digit growth business, with premium-device growth and RF content gains offset by normal integration and price compression.

Diversified Growth Markets generated about $2.9 billion in pro forma fiscal 2026 revenue, up approximately 12% year over year, according to the company. The category includes legacy Skyworks broad markets and Qorvo's High Performance Analog and Connectivity and Sensors Group.

Physical AI and connected edge: More than $1.6 billion in fiscal 2026 revenue, including Wi-Fi access points, gateways, IoT devices, industrial automation and robotics.

Defense and aerospace: Approximately $500 million, supported by modernization, space, electronic warfare and satellite constellations.

Data center and networking infrastructure: Approximately $400 million and identified by management as the company's fastest-growing market.

Automotive: Approximately $340 million, benefiting from electrification, connectivity, autonomy and infotainment trends.

Brace said demand in many of these markets exceeds the company's current ability to supply products. During the September quarter, Skyworks secured additional supply and grew its data center business by about 90% year over year, he said.

December Outlook and Integration Plan

For the December quarter, Skyworks expects combined revenue of $1.8 billion to $1.9 billion, with a midpoint of $1.85 billion. The outlook includes approximately $1.07 billion from legacy Skyworks and approximately $780 million from legacy Qorvo. The company said this will be the last quarter it provides a legacy-company revenue split.

Combined September-quarter revenue was approximately $1.98 billion, including an extra week in Qorvo's quarter that contributed about $70 million. At the December outlook midpoint, revenue would decline roughly 7% sequentially, or about 3% excluding the extra week.

Skyworks expects smartphone revenue to decline by a low-teens percentage sequentially, reflecting seasonality, Android softness and the prior quarter's extra week at Qorvo. Diversified Growth Markets revenue is expected to increase by a low-single-digit percentage sequentially despite the extra week, led by data center and defense. The category is expected to represent more than 40% of sales.

The company forecast non-GAAP gross margin of 46% to 48%, non-GAAP operating expenses of $465 million to $505 million, and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $1.25 at the revenue midpoint. It expects approximately $50 million of other expense, mainly from a full quarter of interest expense on acquisition financing.

Synergies and Long-Term Targets

Skyworks reiterated its expectation for at least $500 million in annual cost synergies from the Qorvo combination. Roughly two-thirds are expected to come from operating expenses and one-third from cost of goods sold.

Management expects approximately $150 million of operating-expense synergies in fiscal 2027 and an annualized exit run rate of approximately $250 million to $300 million. The majority of earnings benefits are expected in the second half of fiscal 2027. Brace said operating-expense savings should arrive first, while factory consolidation and other manufacturing actions will cause cost-of-goods benefits to build later.

Over the long term, Skyworks is targeting mid- to high-single-digit revenue growth. Within 24 to 36 months of closing the transaction, the company is targeting non-GAAP gross margin of 50% to 55%, non-GAAP operating margin of 30% to 35%, and adjusted EBITDA margin of 35% to 40%.

Chief Financial Officer Philip Carter said the company maintains a bias toward share repurchases while also seeking flexibility to build its cash balance following the acquisition financing. He said Skyworks would remain disciplined on accretive acquisitions that could improve gross margins and diversify its revenue base.

About Skyworks Solutions (NASDAQ:SWKS)

Skyworks Solutions, Inc (NASDAQ: SWKS) is a semiconductor company that designs and manufactures high-performance analog and mixed-signal products for wireless connectivity applications. Its portfolio includes radio-frequency front-end modules, amplifiers, filters, switches, antenna tuners, and other integrated solutions used to transmit, receive, and manage wireless signals.

The company serves a range of markets, including smartphones and other mobile devices, automotive systems, industrial equipment, home automation, medical devices, aerospace, and defense.

news.Title: 華邦電法說會行情失靈！盤中挫逾3％刷5個月最低 3萬多人「帳面1張蒸發9萬元」
news.Content:
記憶體大廠華邦電（2344）昨日舉行法說會，公布第3季稅後純益達354億元、年增逾12倍，單季EPS高達 7.58元，大賺超過半個股本，符合市場預期。但受「利多出盡」與第4季展望趨緩影響，今（4）日股價短暫上演慶祝行情後，由紅翻黑，最低觸及140.5％元，寫下5月28日以來、逾5個月盤中最低價，和 6月22日高點233.5元相比，短短5個月內下跌近4成，3萬多人追在高點，帳上一張已蒸發9.15萬元。分析師表示，短線主要受到PC消費需求放緩及明年記憶體漲幅收斂影響，使市場趨於觀望，不過，目前記憶體三雄本益比不到5倍、評價極度便宜，投資人可把握拉回時機逢低布局。

華邦電今天盤中向上衝高至148元即遭拋壓翻黑，最低下探140.5元，跌3.8％，股價寫下5個月盤中最低價。

回顧華邦電今年6月22日盤中最高233.5元，當周受益人數46萬3,762人，和前一周的42萬7,925人相比，增加3萬5837人，假設這3萬多人都追在高點，如今隨著華邦電失守200元關卡，又創5個月最低，帳上已蒸發9.15萬元。

針對華邦電「強勁財報難擋股價拉回」的現象，國泰證期顧問處協理郭經緯分析，主要受限於兩大隱憂：

第一，第4季營運動能趨緩

華邦電總經理陳沛銘於法說會中坦言，儘管AI需求旺盛，但受到PC等消費性電子需求放緩影響，第4季公司營運成長動能將相對平緩。

第二， 記憶體報價漲幅面臨收斂

陳沛銘雖指出明年記憶體市場依然供不應求，但調研機構與法人預估，包括NAND Flash與 DRAM（DDR）明年全年的價格漲幅，將從今年的倍數暴漲收斂至20%至30%左右。在報價漲幅趨緩下，短線股價難免受壓。

南亞科營收連 12 個月創新高也不漲

此外，DRAM 大廠南亞科（2408）昨日才公告 10 月合併營收達464.76億元，年增 487.73%），已連續12個月改寫單月歷史新高，且總經理李培瑛日前於法說會強調，第 4 季DRAM平均銷售單價（ASP）與毛利率將持續上漲，AI帶動的供需缺口非常大。但今日南亞科股價同樣不改頹勢，盤中最低觸及400.5元、重挫2.55%。

旺宏（2337）盤中雖一度大漲3.4%衝上91.3元，隨後也由紅翻黑下探87.6元，9字頭大關得而復失。

郭經緯指出，旺宏主攻利基型記憶體，南亞科則集中於DDR4與DDR5產品。儘管短線市場因報價漲幅收斂而進入觀望，但從估值角度來看，目前記憶體三雄的股價均處於歷史低檔，以明年預估獲利計算，本益比甚至不到 5 倍，「股價整體評價相當便宜」。

郭經緯進一步補充，雖然記憶體價格暴漲期過去，使族群股價短線轉為「區間操作」，但華邦電與南亞科題材後勁仍強，最大的潛在利多在於「高殖利率」。

由於兩家公司今年獲利均出現爆發性成長，若以過去的現金股利發放率推算，華邦電與南亞科明年的現金股息殖利率均有機會突破 10%。預計到了明年上半年，將展現強大的配息吸引力，進一步吸引高股息 ETF 與被動型資金進駐卡位。因此，在企業獲利持續向上、本益比偏低且有超高殖利率護體下，建議長線投資人無須過度悲觀，可把握股價拉回時機逢低分批布局。

陳依旻／財經特派記者副組長，主跑央行、證交所、投信投顧等

news.Title: 《DJ在線》客戶搶簽長約，台記憶體三廠態度不同
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-04 09:02:17 周佩宇 發佈

記憶體客戶爭取供貨保障，長期供貨協議（LTA）也從採購安排，延伸成原廠擴產與投資的重要依據，不過南亞科（2408）、華邦電（2344）及旺宏（2337）的做法並不一致，但都強調，長約是否能連結客戶需求、設備投資與產品路線，比單純追求合約年限更重要。南亞科已有五至七成長約覆蓋，華邦正為新廠洽談搭配預付款的策略合作，旺宏目前則仍未簽訂LTA。

南亞科的長約已進入實際履約與續約階段。公司目前LTA覆蓋率約50%至70%，期間從一季至三年，客戶積極爭取延長供應期限。第三季售價大幅上升，也反映部分過去低價議定的舊約完成交貨後，開始適用新的合約價格，顯示長約雖能增加供需能見度，議價時點與續約安排仍會影響獲利反映速度。

後續擴建則以有客戶長約支持的AI專案為主要目標，林口5A廠預計明(2027)年第一季裝機，2028年底月投片目標3萬片、2030年底達5萬片；設備交期延長、安裝與驗證均需時間，現階段取得的長期需求，將分階段轉成未來供給。

華邦電則將長約與新廠設備投資直接連結。公司表示，希望選擇數家產品路線相符的策略夥伴，涵蓋2029年Module B新產能開出後至2032年的需求，目前有意洽談者已超過10家。合作模式包含客戶先支付訂金或預付款，支應設備投資，再由未來產品供應回饋，各家條件分別協商；例如車用客戶由LPDDR4轉向LPDDR5，若與華邦電未來路線一致，就更有建立長期合作的基礎。供給端則採分階段建置，這次核准731億元資本支出，涵蓋土建、機電及長交期設備，尚未包含全部設備支出，Module B月產6萬片也不會一次到位。這種安排將客戶未來用量、產品轉換與擴產節奏一起考量，也讓華邦電能提前處理設備採購及資金需求。

旺宏則保留不同選擇，董事長吳敏求提到，雖有許多客戶上門洽談，然仍未與任何一家簽訂LTA，因不把長約本身視為保障，更重視每份合約是否公平、互利，並持續優先服務長期合作客戶。而旺宏的擴產瓶頸仍在設備交期，他透露將拜訪設備商催交貨，而增加供給也不排除透過購併或與其他廠商合作。目前擴產規畫首階段新增產能會在2027年下半年量產，後續158億元投資的設備、預計2027年下半年至年底到位，量產落在2028年。

旺宏擴產評估購併、合作，接班人選已定

news.Title: 《DJ在線》AI排擠效應，台廠攻記憶體缺口策略分化
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-04 09:02:13 周佩宇 發佈

記憶體供給吃緊，台灣三家原廠的投資與產品取捨也逐漸拉開差異。從最新今(2026)年第三季法說會及會後採訪來看，南亞科（2408）維持跨世代DRAM供應，保留DDR4轉向DDR5的彈性；華邦電（2344）以DDR4、LPDDR4為近期主力，下一步低功耗產品瞄準LPDDR5；旺宏（2337）則將新增產能集中於NAND與eMMC，NOR則轉向高容量及高可靠度應用。三原廠共同面對大廠產品升級留下的供給缺口，但資源投入並未走向同一條路。

南亞科的策略是兼顧既有客戶與新世代產品。公司第三季DDR4與LPDDR4合計占產品營收逾六成，DDR5約一成；雖有能力依需求將DDR5比重提高至四成，惟目前DDR4客戶需求仍強，尚無大幅調整必要。公司也指出，DDR4、LPDDR4整體市場雖逐步縮小，剩餘需求相對仍大，依然具有經營空間，且應用從PC、車用及工業，延伸至伺服器、網通、儲存與系統管理。公司也同步拓展客製化AI記憶體，目前AI基礎設施相關營收已超過兩成，後續成長方向是增加高容量、高頻寬及客製化產品，但也不會棄守仍缺貨的成熟世代。

華邦電則更強調產品與客戶長期路線的契合。公司表示，現階段DDR4缺口已相當可觀，因此不必積極搶進標準型DDR5，後續低功耗產品規劃由LPDDR4走向LPDDR5，尤其重視車用等生命週期較長的需求。車用、工業客戶採用特定記憶體後，轉換不易，長期供貨能力因而成為爭取合作的重要條件；伺服器與基礎架構客戶也是新增需求來源。支撐這條路線的是20奈米DDR4、LPDDR4，以及已開始放量、預期明年顯著增加營收貢獻的16奈米製程。Flash方面，華邦持續提高高容量NOR與24奈米產品貢獻，AI需求除伺服器運算，也涵蓋交換器及SmartNIC等網通設備。

旺宏相對加重NAND的重要性，尤其是eMMC。公司第三季NAND相關業務含eMMC占營收47%，略高於NOR的46%，其中eMMC營收季增27%。董事長吳敏求說明，大廠淡出部分低容量NAND帶來承接機會，然既有產能卻有限，因此新增產能將投入NAND、eMMC，部分原供NOR使用的產能也轉往NAND；明年eMMC以96層3D NAND為主力，藉製程集中與較佳獲利能力提高資源效率。市場選擇上，目前NAND含eMMC仍以通訊應用為大宗，第三季占比52%，工業、車用等長期需求亦持續布局；NOR則保留資料中心、太空通訊、醫療及車用等市場，高容量產品仍持續開發。

由此可見，三家產品分化的重點，在於選擇哪些缺口值得持續投資、哪些客戶值得保留產能；南亞科與華邦在DDR4、LPDDR4仍有重疊，華邦與旺宏也同樣經營NOR，但各自優先投入的製程、產品與新增產能已有差異。

news.Title: 智原推強化版乙太網路PHY IP，攻AI智慧製造等應用
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-04 09:01:31 新聞中心 發佈

智原(3035)昨(3)日發表支援EtherCAT的強化版10/100乙太網路PHY IP解決方案於聯電(2303)製程，滿足AI智慧製造、工業自動化與人形機器人對即時通訊及同步運動控制日益增長的需求。公司指出，此預先驗證IP支援少於100微秒的EtherCAT傳輸時間，並透過EtherCAT分散式時鐘(Distributed Clocks, DC)實現少於0.1微秒的同步精度，同時通過嚴謹的ETG.7000合規性及IEC 61000-4測試，協助客戶簡化ASIC開發並提升產品開發效率。

此智原Ethernet PHY IP採用DSP架構，結合穩健的類比電路設計，提供優異的抗雜訊能力，並能在嚴峻的電氣干擾環境下維持穩定運作。該PHY IP已依據ETG.7000合規性測試規範通過EtherCAT裝置相容性及網路互通性測試，以及涵蓋靜電放電(ESD)、輻射射頻(RF)、電氣快速瞬變/脈衝群(EFT/Burst) 、突波(Surge)及傳導射頻(Conducted RF)等干擾的關鍵IEC 61000-4電磁相容性(EMC)測試。其可靠度亦透過長達一小時以上的電快速瞬變脈衝群抗擾度測試進一步驗證，在電磁閥產生高頻EFT/Burst脈衝的條件下，確認硬體保護機制及通訊完整性。透過IP層級的強化設計完成預先驗證，可協助客戶減少系統層級的設計與驗證工作，並降低開發風險。

智原營運長林世欽表示：「即時連線能力與優異的抗雜訊穩健性，對次世代工業系統至關重要，尤其在AI日益融入製造與實體機器的趨勢下更是如此。智原將EtherCAT相容性與EMC驗證整合於IP層級，協助客戶簡化系統開發，並降低高額的重新驗證風險。未來智原將持續擴展乙太網路IP產品布局，支援工業AI、軟體定義汽車及人形機器人等應用，包括10/100/1000BASE-T1及單對乙太網路(Single Pair Ethernet, SPE)解決方案。」

news.Title: Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX protest NYSE parent's new plan
news.Content:
Elon Musk 's SpaceX (Nasdaq: SPCX) and Tesla (Nasdaq: TSLA), along with Amazon (Nasdaq: AMZN), Netflix (Nasdaq: NTFX), Lam Research (Nasdaq: LRCX), and SoFi Technologies (Nasdaq: SOFI), have finally objected to the tokenization of their stocks on the OKXICE TSV .

OKXICE TSV is a proposed tokenized stock trading platform created by OKXICE, a 50-50 joint venture between the New York Stock Exchange parent company Intercontinental Exchange (NYSE: ICE) and the OKX crypto exchange.

What's behind the objection

Tokenization is the process of using blockchain technology to turn real‑world assets (RWAs) such as stocks, real estate, government bonds, etc. into digital tokens, which can be traded fractionally, 24/7.

While the stock tokens offer traders from outside the U.S. indirect exposure to the American stock market, they don't offer shareholder rights such as ownership, voting, etc., like original stocks do.

It's the Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) innovation exemption issued in September that allows exchanges like OKXICE to offer tokenized U.S. stocks without registering as exchanges.

But the exemption also allows companies to object to their stocks being tokenized by third parties like OKXICE.

The platform's initial notice got published on Oct. 4, and the SEC's rule lets notified companies object to the plan within 30 days. So, companies have until Nov. 3 to object to it.

This is exactly what companies like Tesla and SpaceX did today: exercise their power to protest the tokenized stock plan.

TheStreet Roundtable spoke to Markus Levin, co-founder of XYO, a cryptographic proof network for data and AI, to get insights on the subject.

"I read this as companies objecting to someone else tokenizing their stock rather than to tokenization itself, since a third-party token leaves the issuer with little visibility into who holds its shares or how votes and dividends reach them. "said Levin. I'd expect most of them to tokenize their own stock through their transfer agents once there's a clear standard for keeping the token and the shareholder register in sync," he added.

news.Title: Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) Tops Q4 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
news.Content:
Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) came out with quarterly earnings of $1.28 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.27 per share. This compares to earnings of $1.76 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +0.79%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this chipmaker would post earnings of $1.03 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.08, delivering a surprise of +4.85%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

Skyworks, which belongs to the Zacks Semiconductors - Radio Frequency industry, posted revenues of $1.05 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.49%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.1 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

Skyworks shares have added about 34.3% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 10.2%.

What's Next for Skyworks?

While Skyworks has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for Skyworks was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $1.30 on $1.05 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $5.18 on $4.06 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Story Continues

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Semiconductors - Radio Frequency is currently in the bottom 12% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

Another stock from the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector, nLight (LASR), has yet to report results for the quarter ended September 2026. The results are expected to be released on November 5.

This laser maker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.06 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of -25%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

nLight's revenues are expected to be $67.96 million, up 1.8% from the year-ago quarter.

STMicroelectronics introduced the STM32A microcontroller family for automotive and high-safety applications, spanning entry-level vehicle nodes through ASIL D-capable zonal endpoints. The lineup is also intended for industrial automation, robotics, energy systems and infrastructure.

ST launched the STM32G5 and STM32H7P microcontrollers for motor control, digital power, signal processing and edge AI. The H7P combines a Cortex-M7 processor, DSP accelerator and 82-GOPS neural accelerator, while the G5 emphasizes higher performance, advanced peripherals and post-quantum security support.

The company expanded its edge-AI strategy through Arm and NVIDIA partnerships, new STM32Cube development tools and updated AI software for model discovery, customization, benchmarking and data preparation. ST also announced STM32Cube for Agentic AI, designed to help coding assistants use STM32-specific development context.

STMicroelectronics Could Reach New Highs—Here's What Needs to Happen

STMicroelectronics (NYSE:STM) used its STM32 Summit in Silicon Valley to outline a "technology convergence" strategy for embedded systems and introduce new microcontroller families and software tools aimed at automotive, industrial automation, robotics, digital power and edge artificial intelligence applications.

The company said its unified STM32 MCU platform is intended to help developers reuse software, tools and intellectual property across product families and markets as systems become more connected, software-defined, security-focused and capable of autonomous operation. ST said the platform is supported by consistent Arm Cortex-M-based architectures, the STM32Cube ecosystem, shared process technologies and a supply chain it manages internally.

→ L3Harris Stock Took a Beating—Is a 20% Rebound Next?

Apple, Meta, and SpaceX Are Driving a Device Boom—These 3 Stocks Could Benefit

According to the company, the STM32 developer ecosystem includes close to 2 million developers, while its ST Community receives more than 300,000 visitors per month. ST also said it has shipped more than 20 billion STM32 devices.

Arm partnership and physical AI

Arm Executive Vice President of the Physical AI Business Unit Drew Henry said ST will be a lead partner in defining the future Cortex-M roadmap, alongside Cadence as a design partner. Henry said Arm has shipped more than 100 billion Cortex-M devices and sees physical AI as a potential $200 billion compute market by the middle of the next decade.

Story Continues

→ LyondellBasell's Dividend Looks Safer, But a New Risk Could Change That

Industrial Chips Are in Rally Mode—5 Ways to Play

"We believe that this is a $200 billion compute market in the middle of next decade or so," Henry said, referring to systems that apply AI to agriculture, manufacturing, transportation and other real-world environments.

ST said it is combining Arm CPUs, its neural accelerators and more than a decade of MCU AI software experience for edge AI workloads. The company also highlighted deterministic Ethernet connectivity, integrated security features including SHA accelerators and post-quantum cryptography libraries, and safety-focused hardware and software support.

STM32A expands into automotive and safety applications

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

A central product announcement was the STM32A series, which ST described as a new line combining its general-purpose and automotive microcontroller experience. The series is designed for automotive and high-safety embedded applications, including industrial automation, robotics, energy systems and infrastructure.

ST unveiled the initial three-product roadmap:

STM32A4: Intended for entry-level automotive nodes, including distributed sensing, actuation, doors, windows, lighting and local controls. ST said the devices will offer low cost, compact memory, cryptographic support and LIN implementation.

STM32A5: Targeted at body and comfort-control functions, with up to 4 MB of memory, enhanced security and safety support up to ASIL B. ST said the devices are also suited to mid-range safety-critical industrial, robotics and energy applications.

STM32A9: Intended for higher-function zonal vehicle endpoints, with real-time control, low-latency and Ethernet-oriented connectivity, plus safety support up to ASIL D. ST said its split-lock core architecture can prioritize ASIL D operation or provide twice the ASIL B performance when ASIL D is not required.

The company said the STM32A family will provide continuity with STM32-compatible IP, software concepts, tools and the STM32Cube ecosystem while addressing automotive-grade qualification, functional safety, security and longer product lifecycles.

NVIDIA Vice President of Robotics and Edge AI Deepu Talla discussed the companies' work around robotics and the Holoscan Sensor Bridge, which enables sensor and actuator connectivity over Ethernet. ST said it plans to release Holoscan Sensor Bridge software as a native component of the STM32Cube ecosystem in coming months and intends to develop simulation libraries for its sensor, MEMS, microcontroller and actuation portfolios.

STM32G5 and STM32H7P product launches

ST also launched the STM32G5, a general-purpose mixed-signal microcontroller based on an Arm Cortex-M33 running at up to 280 MHz. The company said the device delivers a CoreMark score more than double that of the STM32G4 and is designed for motor control and digital power applications.

Versions aimed at digital power will include additional high-resolution timers, while motor-control versions will provide more analog peripherals, ST said. Other cited capabilities include a 111-picosecond timer resolution, a position encoder, a programmable logic array with 16 logic elements, a 5-megasample-per-second analog-to-digital converter and pseudo-differential mode for signal-to-noise performance.

The STM32G5 targets SESIP Level 3 and PSA Certified Level 3 security certifications and supports post-quantum cryptographic libraries, according to ST. Initial devices, Nucleo boards and Discovery kits are available, while ST said a dual-core version is being developed for release next year.

Ram Kumar of ST introduced the STM32H7P, describing it as the company's first STM32H7 combining a Cortex-M7 processor, a Hardware Signal Processor DSP accelerator and an 82-GOPS Neural-ART accelerator. The microcontroller operates at up to 520 MHz and delivers a CoreMark score of nearly 2,700, which Kumar said is 150% above most competing solutions.

The STM32H7P includes high-resolution timers, comparators and twice the flash memory of a 1 MB STM32H7 at roughly the same price, according to ST. Kumar said the device is aimed at digital power, digital signal processing and edge AI applications, and can operate in industrial environments up to 105 degrees Celsius through exposed-pad packaging.

AI development software update

ST also updated its AI software offering. Miguel Castro, head of AI marketing and strategy for the Americas, said the company is replacing its Model Zoo interface with Model Explorer, Model Factory and Model Bench tools for discovering, customizing and benchmarking AI models. It also introduced Dataset Factory for organizing and cleaning data.

In addition, ST announced STM32Cube for Agentic AI, a tool intended to provide coding assistants with STM32 documentation, guidelines, examples and other development context. Castro said early experiments reduced token usage by 93% for a blinking-light application, while typical configurations are expected to reduce token usage by roughly 50% to 60%.

About STMicroelectronics (NYSE:STM)

STMicroelectronics N.V. (NYSE: STM) is a global semiconductor company that designs, develops, manufactures and markets a broad range of integrated circuits and other semiconductor products. Its offerings support applications in automotive, industrial, personal electronics, communications equipment and computer systems.

The company's product portfolio includes microcontrollers, analog and power semiconductors, sensors, microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), connectivity products and automotive chips.

news.Title: Lam Research Sees Strong 2027 Growth as Shareholders Back Board, Pay Plan
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Lam Research Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

Shareholders approved all four key voting outcomes: They elected Lam Research's 10 director nominees, approved executive compensation, ratified KPMG as fiscal 2027 auditor, and rejected a proposal to lower the ownership threshold for calling special meetings.

Lam expects strong 2027 semiconductor-equipment demand. The company projects wafer fabrication equipment spending will exceed $200 billion, up about 30%, as 10 major fabs become available to receive equipment and clean-room constraints ease.

CEO Tim Archer cited gate-all-around transistors, EUV and high-NA EUV lithography, backside power delivery, and advanced packaging as long-term growth drivers because these technologies require intensive etch and deposition processes.

Lam Research's Earnings Beat Wasn't the Real Story—Its 2027 Outlook Was

Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) stockholders elected all 10 director nominees, approved the company's executive compensation plan on an advisory basis and ratified KPMG LLP as its independent auditor for fiscal 2027 at the company's 2026 annual meeting.

The virtual meeting, chaired by Board Chair Abhi Talwalkar, did not include a formal business update because Lam had provided its most recent update during its Oct. 21 earnings release call. Talwalkar said the meeting's purpose was to vote on four proposals outlined in the company's proxy materials.

→ L3Harris Stock Took a Beating—Is a 20% Rebound Next?

From High Dividend Growth to High Yield, These 3 Stocks Just Boosted Dividend Payouts

Corporate Secretary Ava Harter reported that a quorum was present. Following the vote, Harter said preliminary results showed that stockholders had:

Elected all 10 board nominees.

Approved the advisory "say-on-pay" vote covering named executive officer compensation.

Ratified KPMG LLP as Lam's independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal 2027.

Rejected a stockholder proposal concerning the right to call special stockholder meetings.

Lam said it expects to report final voting results in a Form 8-K filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission within four business days.

Special Meeting Proposal Rejected

→ LyondellBasell's Dividend Looks Safer, But a New Risk Could Change That

Analysts Just Raised Price Targets On These 3 Semiconductor Equipment Stocks

The shareholder proposal, presented by stockholder John Chevedden, called on Lam's board to amend the company's governing documents to allow holders of a combined 10% of outstanding common stock to call a special stockholder meeting.

Story Continues

Chevedden argued that Lam's current rules create significant barriers by requiring 20% support and excluding a substantial block of shares from being included in the qualifying group. He said the requested change would create an "attainable shareholder right" to call a special meeting.

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

Harter said the board recommended that stockholders vote against the proposal for the reasons included in the company's proxy statement. The proposal was not approved.

CEO Cites Demand From Technology Transitions

During a post-meeting question-and-answer session, President and Chief Executive Officer Tim Archer discussed semiconductor technology transitions, including gate-all-around transistor architectures and the implementation of extreme ultraviolet, or EUV, and high-numerical-aperture EUV lithography.

Archer said these transitions are "extremely etch and deposition intensive," making them well suited to Lam's product portfolio and driving significant demand for its equipment.

He also identified backside power delivery and advanced packaging as potential long-term growth drivers. Archer acknowledged that supply-chain issues have constrained the pace of industry growth, but said Lam is working around those challenges.

Fiscal 2027 Industry Outlook

Archer said customer fabrication-plant utilization rates remain very high. He noted that limited clean-room space was one of the constraints on industry growth during the current year because chipmakers needed more space to install equipment and expand production.

That constraint is expected to ease somewhat in 2027, according to Archer, who said Lam expects 10 tier-one fabs to open and become available to receive equipment during the year.

Lam's outlook, as previously discussed on its latest earnings call, calls for wafer fabrication equipment spending to exceed $200 billion in 2027, representing approximately 30% growth from the current year. Archer added that Lam believes its addressable markets are growing faster than the broader semiconductor equipment industry and said 2027 appears positioned to be another strong growth year for the company.

About Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX)

Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX) is a semiconductor equipment company that develops and manufactures systems used to fabricate integrated circuits. Its technologies support key stages of wafer processing, helping semiconductor manufacturers create the increasingly complex structures found in memory, logic and other types of chips.

The company's product portfolio includes etch systems, which selectively remove materials from wafers; deposition systems, which apply thin films; and cleaning solutions used to remove contaminants and residue during manufacturing.

news.Title: SIMO Earnings Surge as Enterprise and AI Storage Drive New Momentum
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO delivered a sharp third-quarter earnings acceleration as enterprise, automotive and artificial intelligence storage became larger contributors to growth. The results strengthen the case that its revenue mix is moving beyond traditional consumer storage controllers.

The key question is whether that shift can support a more durable earnings profile. Current guidance, expanding solutions revenue and new enterprise products point to broader growth drivers, though execution and consumer-market risks remain.

SIMO's Third Quarter Set New Financial Highs

Third-quarter 2026 revenues reached $560.2 million, up 131% year over year and 24% sequentially. Non-GAAP earnings of $4.35 per American depositary share beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.30 by 31.82% and increased 335% from the year-ago period.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Profitability also improved materially. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 32.1% from 15.8% a year earlier, while gross margin rose to 53.7% from 48.7%. The combination of higher volumes and a richer product mix helped lift operating leverage.

Silicon Motion's Solutions Business is Surging

Ferri and boot-drive solution sales climbed 75-80% sequentially in the third quarter, supported by automotive, edge artificial intelligence and enterprise demand. Solutions accounted for more than 40% of total revenues, and management expects the category could represent roughly half of revenues in 2027.

That mix shift could make Silicon Motion less dependent on consumer controller cycles. Automotive programs generally span three to five years, while enterprise boot-drive opportunities provide another source of longer-duration demand. Micron Technology, Inc. MU is also expanding high-capacity data-center solid-state drive offerings for artificial intelligence, cloud and hyperscale workloads, underscoring the broader storage opportunity tied to data-intensive computing.

SIMO's Fourth-Quarter Guidance Extends the Trend

Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $588 million to $616 million, implying sequential growth of 5%-10%. Non-GAAP gross margin is projected at 54%-55%, while operating margin is expected to reach 36%-37%.

The outlook suggests the third-quarter improvement is carrying into year-end rather than fading immediately after a record period. For 2027, management expects revenue growth of at least 40% and gross margins in the low-to-mid-50% range, supported by rising contributions from enterprise controllers and Ferri automotive solutions.

Story Continues

Silicon Motion Is Building for the Next AI Cycle

Silicon Motion taped out its 4-nanometer PCIe Gen6 MonTitan controller in the third quarter, with sampling scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. The product targets hyperscalers and cloud service providers and is designed for both TLC-based compute storage and QLC-based data storage.

Four NAND makers have begun producing 2-terabit QLC dies, with broader availability expected by the end of 2027. That supply expansion could support higher-capacity enterprise storage deployments. Seagate Technology Holdings plc STX is likewise positioning its mass-capacity storage portfolio around rising artificial intelligence and cloud data demand, showing that infrastructure spending is broadening across storage technologies.

SIMO's Ratings Temper the Earnings Excitement

The latest quarter supports the view that Silicon Motion is becoming a more diversified storage supplier, but the transition is not yet complete. Consumer weakness, customer qualification requirements and supply-chain constraints still create uncertainty around how smoothly the enterprise ramp develops.

SIMO currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). It also has a Value Score of D and Momentum Score of D, along with a Growth Score of F and VGM Score of F. Because the Style Scores complement the Zacks Rank, these weaker grades suggest a more measured near-term stance even as the company's enterprise and artificial intelligence exposure expands. news.Title: SIMO Stock Falls 33.5% in a Month as Growth Meets Execution Risks
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO shares have fallen 33.5% over the past four weeks, a sharp reversal despite record revenues and expanding exposure to enterprise and AI storage. The drop raises the question of whether valuation now better reflects the company's growth prospects.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The answer is not straightforward. Enterprise diversification, automotive demand and higher-value storage products support the outlook, but consumer weakness, qualification requirements and supply-chain constraints leave execution risk elevated.

SIMO's Record Growth Contrasts With the Sell-Off

Third-quarter 2026 revenues surged 131% year over year to about $560 million, marking a fourth consecutive quarter of record revenues. Non-GAAP earnings per ADS rose 335% to $4.35, while operating margin expanded to 32.1%.

The quarter also exceeded the Zacks Consensus Estimate on both the top and bottom lines. Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $588-$616 million, with non-GAAP operating margin rising to 36%-37%.

Silicon Motion's Enterprise Mix Is Expanding

Ferri automotive and enterprise boot-drive solutions grew more than 75% sequentially and represented more than 40% of third-quarter revenues. Management indicated that the solutions business could reach roughly half of revenues in 2027.

That shift increases exposure to longer-duration programs and higher-value storage opportunities. Micron Technology, Inc. MU, which offers DRAM, NAND and data-center SSDs, illustrates the broader memory and storage ecosystem in which enterprise demand is expanding.

SIMO Faces Persistent Consumer Pressure

Elevated NAND and DRAM prices are pressuring smartphone and PC affordability. eMMC and UFS controller revenues declined modestly sequentially in the third quarter, and management expects near-term revenues in that business to remain relatively flat.

SSD controller revenues are also expected to be flat to slightly lower sequentially in the fourth quarter. These trends show that enterprise growth is offsetting, rather than eliminating, weakness in established consumer-facing markets.

Silicon Motion Must Execute on Enterprise Ramps

Enterprise expansion depends on customer qualifications, production ramps and component availability. MonTitan is scaling across seven announced customers, while Silicon Motion's 4-nanometer PCIe Gen6 MonTitan controller is scheduled to begin sampling in the first quarter of 2027.

Near-CPU boot-drive opportunities add another execution layer because customized firmware and customer-specific features are required. Seagate Technology Holdings PLC STX, whose portfolio includes cloud, edge and data-center storage products, provides another reference point for the scale and complexity of enterprise storage markets.

Story Continues

SIMO's Valuation Adds Context to the Decline

SIMO trades at 12.1X forward 12-month earnings, below its five-year median of 19.4X but above the Zacks sub-industry's 9.4X. The lower multiple versus its own history reflects a materially different valuation backdrop after the recent share-price pullback.

The discount to SIMO's historical median may look more attractive if enterprise ramps progress as planned. Still, the premium to the sub-industry means investors are not being offered a uniformly cheap valuation relative to peers.

SIMO's Signals Still Favor a Cautious View

SIMO's growth and valuation setup remains mixed. Record operating performance and enterprise diversification support the longer-term case, while consumer pressure and execution requirements argue against treating the 33.5% decline alone as a buy signal.

The stock currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). It has a Value Score of D and Momentum Score of D, along with a Growth Score of F and VGM Score of F. Since the Style Scores are designed to complement the Zacks Rank, these weaker grades support a measured stance despite the company's strong recent fundamental growth. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Q3 Earnings & JOLTS Report on Midterm Voting Day
news.Content:
Tuesday, November 3rd, 2026

Pre-market futures are mixed ahead of the bell, with the Nasdaq building back some of its recent losses on AI-buildout concerns, and a "wait and see" mentality regarding the U.S. midterm elections takes hold. Early voting has seen some 60+ million Americans take to the ballot this year — far ahead of normal levels of midterm voting.

The Dow is selling off a bit this morning, -371 points, while the Nasdaq is +89 at this hour. The S&P 500, as per normal, is splitting the difference, -12 points presently. Crude oil prices are down on two noteworthy events in the Middle East: the U.S. has attacked Iran's Qeshm Island overnight, which is the largest island in the Persian Gulf, and President Trump has announced he will be pulling back $4 billion in payments to Israel by the end of the year.

Q3 Earnings This Morning: PFE, SHOP

Big Pharma staple Pfizer PFE released Q3 results ahead of today's open, posting earnings of $0.87 per share versus expectations of $0.72, for a +20.8% positive earnings surprise. Revenues of $16.58 billion in the quarter outpaced the Zacks consensus by +2.8%. The drugmaker upped guidance on stronger Eliquis sales, but shares are flat pre-market after gaining +23% year to date. For more on PFE's earnings, click here.

E-commerce mainstay Shopify SHOP shares are tumbling -15% in today's early trading, despite modest beats on both top and bottom lines in its Q3 this morning. Earnings of $0.49 per share amounted to a 4-cent outperformance, with revenues of $3.74 billion +0.15% ahead of estimates. The company missed on Gross Merchandise Volume (GMV) and subscription metrics, however. For more on SHOP's earnings, click here.

After today's close, we'll hear from AI chipmaking company Advanced Micro Devices AMD, which is up in today's pre-market and +118% year to date. Analysts are expecting +61.7% earnings growth and +41.89% on revenues. The Lisa Su-run company has not missed on earnings expectations since Q4 2018.

Not to be confused based on similar ticker symbol, agriculture giant Archer Daniels-Midland ADM also reports after today's close. Earnings growth is expected to come in at an excellent +77.2% year over year, with revenues projected up +11.3%. The Zacks Rank #2 (Buy)-rated company is aiming for its eight-straight quarterly earnings beat.

Meanwhile, software firm Skyworks Solutions SWKS reports its fiscal Q4 report after today's close. Following the company's $10 billion Qorvo acquisition, Skyworks looks to report earning down -27.84% year over year, -6.35% on revenues. The company has not missed on bottom-line estimates since Q1 2019.

Story Continues

What to Expect from the Stock Market Today

We won't get any midterm returns until well after today's trading session is over, but we'll make sure to keep abreast of developments throughout the country today. Otherwise, the September print on Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) is expected to remain in-line with the prior month, at +7.1 million job openings.

JOLTS numbers are back to pre-Covid levels, and have been here pretty steadily over the past nearly two years. This is consistent with the "low hire/low fire" employment numbers we've seen elsewhere. Job Quits in August dropped to 3.07 million, at an historically low +1.9% rate. Basically, lots of people remain employed, but fewer are finding opportunities elsewhere. Today's JOLTS figures kicks off the latest "Jobs Week."
